model.name: Commercial Contract
model.purpose: Give agents the context needed to identify, form, read, operate and close a legally binding commercial agreement between two or more parties as a jointly owned record, independent of storage format.
model.scope_statement: Covers the agreement record itself: its identity and classification, the party positions and their authority, how it was concluded and executed, the structure and terms of the agreed text, the obligations and schedule it creates, the record of performance, non-performance, remedy, change, notice and termination, and the governance of that record (provenance, integrity, access, retention, interoperability). Scope is business-to-business commercial contracting, following the HCCH Principles' scope of parties acting in the exercise of their trade or profession. External legal norms, the real-world identity of the parties, procurement award processes and dispute proceedings are referenced, not duplicated.
in_scope: Agreement identity, subject-matter classification and the applicable legal regime declaration
Party positions, their roles, legal identification and signing authority
Formation facts: offer, acceptance, conduct, standard-term incorporation, execution and effectiveness
Addressable clause structure, constituent document set, precedence and authentic language
Commercial terms: price and payment, delivery and risk transfer, warranty, liability and protective terms
Obligations expressed as deontic specifications with bearers, source clauses, violations and reparations
Milestones, due conditions, cure periods and performance/acceptance records
Non-performance, excuse, remedy, amendment, assignment, notice, termination and survival
Record governance: provenance, integrity of the executed text, access, retention, disposition and projections
out_of_scope: Consumer contracts and employment contracts (excluded by the HCCH Principles' commercial scope)
The legal existence, powers and internal governance of the parties themselves (organization/person models)
The procurement or tendering process that precedes award
Conduct of litigation or arbitration proceedings and the resulting awards
Statutory and regulatory norms as such; only their declared applicability to this agreement is in scope
Payment execution, settlement instruments and accounting entries
Transfer of property/title, which CISG Article 4 expressly leaves to the applicable national law
Distributed-ledger execution substrates for smart contracts
Tax determination, transfer pricing and customs classification

boundary_notes.distinction: The tendering, evaluation and award process is owned by the procurement model; UBL separates Tender and Contract Award Notice documents from the resulting contract. Award output composes into a new agreement record here.

The legal entity and its verified identifier (LEI under ISO 17442) live in the party model; this model holds only the party position, its role and the link plus verification evidence. The registry validation flag 'a contract is not an organization' is upheld.

The arbitration or jurisdiction clause, the escalation state and the written-form evidence required by New York Convention Article II are in scope; the proceeding, award and enforcement action are not.

Overriding mandatory rules and statutory regimes (for example CISG applicability, unfair-term controls under the Data Act) are external norms; this model records only the applicability declaration and any opt-out.

Certificate issuance, trusted lists and signature-creation devices belong to the eIDAS trust-service domain; this model records the signature type, assurance level and validation evidence attached to execution.
Specialised agreement types EXTEND this model with domain terms and lifecycle events; their product-specific economics are not duplicated here.

functions.name: Register agreement record
functions.description: Create the jointly owned record for a new agreement with its identifier, party positions, classification and legal frame.
inputs: Party position set with role codes
preconditions: At least two party positions are declared
A commercial-scope assertion exists for every position
Governing law and forum are declared or explicitly marked absent
effects: Agreement identifier is bound and cannot be reassigned
Record enters the pre-effective state
Registration event is written to the audit log with event and ingestion time

functions.name: Verify party identity and signing authority
functions.description: Check each named party against the authoritative registry and confirm the signatory's power to bind within its limits.
preconditions: A party position exists
An authority basis is asserted
effects: Verification observation time is recorded
Authority defect raises an exception state instead of blocking silently

functions.name: Record conclusion and execution
functions.description: Capture the concluding communications or signatures, the effective moment and the signature validation evidence.
inputs: Formation communication set or signed container
preconditions: Party identity and authority verification have been attempted and their results recorded
Any applicable form requirement has been identified
effects: Executed expression digest is fixed and becomes immutable
Record moves to conditional or effective state depending on outstanding conditions

functions.name: Build addressable clause tree
functions.description: Convert the agreed text into a hierarchy of addressable provisions with expression and work identifiers and per-node digests.
preconditions: The manifestation's digest matches the executed expression digest
effects: Clause references become stable across later amendments
Any extraction uncertainty is recorded as provenance, not silently normalised

functions.name: Derive obligation set
functions.description: Produce deontic statements with bearers, conditions, violations and reparations traced to source clauses.
preconditions: Clause tree exists with stable identifiers
Bearer positions are resolvable
effects: Derived rules are marked as derived, never as the normative text
A later amendment invalidates and re-derives the affected rules

functions.name: Evaluate effectiveness and conditions
functions.description: Determine whether conditions precedent are satisfied or waived and compute the current validity state.
preconditions: Execution has been recorded
Each condition has an evidence slot
effects: Obligations become enforceable only after the effectiveness event
Lapse at long-stop date is recorded as an event, not a deletion

functions.name: Monitor due obligations
functions.description: Compute which duties are due, overdue or within a cure period from due conditions and recorded events.
preconditions: Obligations carry due conditions
All timestamps carry seconds and explicit offsets
effects: Status transitions are emitted as events with event and observation time
No status is inferred without an evidenced trigger

functions.name: Record performance and acceptance
functions.description: Attach evidence that a duty was performed, capture measured results and register the counterparty's acceptance decision.
preconditions: The obligation exists and is due or performable
The recording actor is authorised for that party position
effects: Event time and observation time are stored separately
Deemed acceptance is applied only where an agreed rule exists

functions.name: Declare non-performance and elect remedy
functions.description: Register a breach declaration, any asserted excuse, the remedy elected and its quantification.
preconditions: A notice satisfying the contractual notice rules has been issued where required
Any cure period has expired or is expressly waived
effects: Record enters a disputed state that blocks disposition
Remedy election is immutable once notified, subject to a superseding agreed settlement

functions.name: Apply executed amendment
functions.description: Produce a new expression of the agreed text from an executed amendment while retaining the superseded expression.
preconditions: The required variation formality is satisfied and evidenced
The amendment is signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution
effects: Superseded expression is retained and remains addressable
Obligations affected by changed clauses are invalidated and re-derived

functions.name: Issue and track formal notice
functions.description: Send a contractual notice through a permitted channel to the designated address and record dispatch, receipt and consequences.
preconditions: The channel and address are permitted by the contract
The sender is authorised to act for the sending position
effects: Notice periods start running from the deemed receipt time
Failure of delivery evidence marks the notice as contested rather than valid

functions.name: Verify record integrity
functions.description: Re-verify digests, signatures and time stamps over the executed text and dependent artifacts and report divergence.
preconditions: A canonicalisation rule is recorded for each artifact class
effects: Failed verification sets a disputed flag and never deletes the artifact
Verification observation time is recorded separately from the artifact's event time

functions.name: Emit projection to a non-party
functions.description: Generate a reduced view exposing only the elements a declared projection permits, with its omission list and generation time.
preconditions: A valid, unexpired grant covers the requested scope
The projection definition is a governed, versioned artifact
effects: Restricted elements are excluded before serialisation, not filtered afterwards
Every emission is logged with requester, purpose and grant reference

functions.name: Apply retention and disposition
functions.description: Evaluate retention rules, limitation periods and holds, and carry out authorised disposition or redaction with evidence.
inputs: Limitation period for the governing law
preconditions: No hold or dispute is in force over the element
The longest applicable retention or limitation period has expired
effects: Executed text and signature evidence are never hard-deleted while any period runs
Redaction preserves the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control

functions.name: Avoid or terminate
functions.description: End the agreement by notice of avoidance, agreed termination or expiry, releasing future duties while preserving dispute and winding-up clauses and triggering restitution.
preconditions: fundamental breach, Nachfrist failure, agreed termination, or completed performance
notice given where CISG Article 26 requires it
effects: status becomes avoided or terminated
open primary obligations are released subject to damages and restitution

functions.name: Declare breach and fix additional time
functions.description: Record a breach declaration, classify it as fundamental or not, and optionally fix a Nachfrist period or demand adequate assurance.
preconditions: failure to perform or clear future fundamental breach
notice capable of reaching the other party
effects: inconsistent remedies are barred during a running Nachfrist
damages for delay remain available

functions.name: Assign or novate
functions.description: Transfer rights or, with required consent, obligations, and notify the remaining obligor without purporting to move in rem title.
preconditions: contractual assignability or required consent
notice to obligor where effectiveness against the obligor so requires
effects: party positions or payee identity change on the contractual plane only

composition.purpose: Resolve the legal entity occupying a party position and its governed identifier; entity existence and powers stay in the organization model.
Resolve natural persons acting as signatories or agents without duplicating personal data in the contract record.
Verify signing capacity and delegated powers against the constitutional documents recorded there.
An award concluded in the procurement model composes into a new agreement instance here; the tendering documents remain in the procurement model.
An insurance policy is a specialised commercial contract that extends this model with cover, premium and claim structures.
Executed prices may serve as price observations under a contribution agreement; the valuation model reads a projection rather than the terms.
Escalated disputes are heard there; this model holds the clause, the written-form evidence and the escalation state.
Joint ownership of the record and grants over scoped parts of it are administered by the stewardship and access-grant models.
Adds provenance and audit facets to execution, performance, amendment, notice and access events using a standard agent, activity and entity vocabulary.
Align the obligation model to a normative deontic vocabulary for obligations, permissions, prohibitions, violations and reparations.

composition.target: OASIS Akoma Ntoso and its Naming Convention v1.0
composition.purpose: Align clause addressing and versioned expression IRIs to an established legal-document naming convention.
Align exchange projections to interoperable business document types for contracting, ordering and delivery without exposing clause text.
Align formation, performance, non-performance, excuse and remedy terminology to the recognised international contract-law instruments.
Bind the delivery term data element to a governed classifier that requires both a rule code and an edition to be interpretable.

composition.target: Electronic signature and trust service framework
composition.purpose: Resolve signature assurance levels, certificates, time-stamp tokens and trusted-list status used as execution evidence.

owner_package_requirements: Declare a jointly owned record package per agreement instance in which each party position holds an equivalent mirror and joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events; unilateral acts such as notices are writable by their sender alone.
Bind every party position to an authoritative party record and store the identity verification evidence with its observation time before any obligation is derived.
Declare governing law, dispute forum and the retention jurisdiction before clause content is stored, because these determine mandatory rules, limitation periods and deletion limits.
Publish an AGENTS.md bootstrap and a versioned projection catalogue listing every view exposed to non-parties and what each view omits.
dimension.namespace_guidance: Adopt the namespace world.commercialContract under nav path NAV.SOC.ECO.CTR. Agreement expressions and clauses are named with FRBR-style Work and Expression IRIs and persistent clause identifiers so that references survive amendment; never mint contract IRIs under a single party's namespace, because the record is jointly owned. Derived artifacts such as obligation rule sets live in a clearly separate derived subnamespace so they can never be mistaken for the executed text.
registry_links: Global LEI Index for party legal entity identifiers under ISO 17442
ICC Incoterms rule codes with an explicit edition qualifier
Currency and country code lists referenced by the price, place-of-business and jurisdiction elements
Trusted lists of qualified trust service providers for signature and time-stamp validation
UBL document type and business process code lists used by exchange projections

canonicalization_rules: The canonical form is the executed expression: the clause tree with stable identifiers, the party positions, the derived obligation set marked as derived, and a digest over the normative text. PDF, DOCX, HTML, Markdown, JSON, YAML and database rows are manifestations, not the canon.

Timestamps are canonicalised to RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset; the local offset of execution, dispatch and delivery is preserved rather than normalised to Z, because contractual periods run in a stated locality.
Monetary values are canonicalised as an amount plus a currency code, never as formatted strings; quantities carry an explicit unit.
Parties are canonicalised to a position identifier plus a governed entity identifier, never to a display name; trade terms are canonicalised as code plus edition plus named place.
patch_rules: A patch that changes normative text is valid only if it carries an executed amendment instrument signed at an assurance level no lower than the original execution.
Patches are append-only: superseded expressions are retained and remain addressable by their expression IRI; no in-place overwrite of executed content is permitted.
Editorial or metadata patches must be flagged non-normative and must not change the digest of the executed expression; if the digest would change, the change is an amendment, not a patch.
Every patch records the actor, the reason, the event time at which the change takes effect and the ingestion time at which it was recorded, as distinct values.
compatibility_rules: Adding optional findings, data elements or projections is backward compatible; changing the clause identity scheme, the deontic vocabulary, the party role vocabulary or the identity priority is breaking and requires a major version.
Relationships to CISG, UNIDROIT, Incoterms, UBL, LegalRuleML and Akoma Ntoso are published as alignments with a declared claim level; a conformance claim requires cited test evidence.
Consumers must tolerate unknown clause classes, unknown remedy kinds and unknown notice kinds rather than rejecting the record, and must not infer absence of a term from absence of a code.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system identifier issued by the system of record for the agreement, such as the contract register number of the register the parties have jointly designated as authoritative, where such an identifier exists and is agreed by all parties
Governed global identifier or IRI, such as a FRBR-style Akoma Ntoso expression IRI for the executed text or an ISO 17442 legal entity identifier for a party occupying a position
UUID or ULID minted by the adopting Dimension, recorded together with the minting authority and mint time, used only where neither a master-system nor a governed identifier is available
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: All time values are RFC 3339 date-times carrying seconds and an explicit numeric offset or Z; the local offset of execution, dispatch, delivery and performance is preserved because contractual periods run in a stated locality. Event time, meaning the moment the contractual fact occurred or took effect, is recorded separately from observation or ingestion time, meaning the moment the record captured it, whenever the two can differ. Where UTC is known but the local offset is not, use -00:00 rather than Z. A date is never used as an identifier.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Serial artifacts, namely amendments, notices, performance records, verification records, manifests, dispositions and log segments, are numbered with a zero-padded monotonic sequence scoped to the agreement identifier and the artifact class, for example agreement-id/amendment/0003. Sequence numbers are never reused, never renumbered on amendment and never encode a date; any effective date is carried as a separate field.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Every executed or issued artifact carries a digest over its canonical bytes with a named algorithm, the signature or seal evidence relied on at execution, and an attributable time stamp. The digest of the executed expression is immutable for the life of the record. Verification failure sets a disputed flag, notifies all party positions and is written to the audit log; it never causes deletion or silent replacement of the artifact.

policies: Joint record policy: the agreement record is jointly owned by the party positions; joint facts change only on jointly evidenced events, while unilateral acts are attributable to their sender and remain contestable by the counterparty.
Alignment-not-conformance policy: relationships to external standards are recorded as alignments with an explicit claim level; a conformance claim without cited test evidence is a defect.

Derived-content policy: obligation rule sets, schedules, scorecards and summaries are marked as derived and carry provenance back to source clauses; they never acquire normative status over the executed text.
Minimisation policy: any view issued to a non-party exposes only what its versioned projection definition permits and publishes the list of what it omits.

Preservation policy: retention rules are suspended by a dispute or legal hold; personal data inside executed evidence is redacted in place with preserved digests rather than destroyed while any limitation period runs.
Party-mirror policy: each party holds the full agreement record; joint facts change only by joint events or jointly authorized amendments.

Form-and-signature policy: writing and signature requirements follow the applicable instrument (CISG Articles 11–13 and 96, UCC § 2-201, MLEC/MLES) and any insisted particular form under UNIDROIT Article 2.1.13.
Disclosure-minimisation policy: existence and performance standing may be disclosed to consented credit or rating consumers; clause text and prices are omitted from public summaries.
No-unilateral-delete policy: the joint record is not deleted by a single party's CRUD delete; retention, legal hold and limitation clocks govern archive and redaction.

read: Every party position may read the complete joint record, including clause text, obligations and performance history.
Non-parties read only through a declared projection, and the projection definition is itself a governed, versioned artifact.
Reads of restricted findings such as price terms, liability caps and personal data are logged with requester identity, purpose and grant reference.
create: Creating an agreement record requires at least two party positions, a subject-matter class, a governing-law declaration and a recorded conclusion or execution event with evidence.
Clause, obligation, milestone, performance, notice and amendment records may be created only under an existing agreement identifier.
Creation resolves the identifier through the identity priority; a Dimension-minted surrogate is permitted only with recorded minting authority and mint time.
update: Changes to normative content require an executed amendment artifact; the prior expression is retained and stays addressable.
Operational changes such as performance, notices, status transitions and disclosures are recorded as append-only events, never as in-place edits.
Metadata corrections are recorded as non-normative patches carrying actor, reason, event time and ingestion time, and must not alter the executed expression digest.
delete: Hard deletion of executed text, signature evidence, notices or performance evidence is prohibited while any limitation period, statutory retention duty or legal hold applies.
Personal data within executed evidence may be redacted in place, with a redaction record preserving the digest of the unredacted expression under separate control.
Disposition after retention expiry follows an approved disposition authority and is itself recorded as an event with its authorising instrument.

roles.name: Party record steward
responsibilities: Maintain one party's mirror of the joint record and keep it reconciled with the counterparty's mirror
Escalate divergence between mirrors as a dispute rather than resolving it unilaterally

roles.name: Authorised representative
responsibilities: Execute, amend, assign or terminate on behalf of a party within recorded authority limits
Ensure the authority instrument relied on is current and evidenced at the time of signing

roles.name: Contract text custodian
responsibilities: Maintain the clause tree, expression versions, document manifest and precedence order
Preserve superseded expressions and the identifier map that links them

roles.name: Performance recorder and verifier
responsibilities: Record performance events, measured values and acceptance decisions with event and observation times
Attach evidence and flag deemed acceptance only where an agreed rule exists

roles.name: Access and disclosure administrator
responsibilities: Issue, scope and expire grants over bundles, layers, findings and artifacts
Apply redaction rules and log every disclosure with purpose and legal basis

roles.name: Records and retention officer
responsibilities: Apply retention rules, limitation periods and legal holds and block disposition while any is in force
Execute and evidence authorised disposition or redaction

access.default_rule: Deny by default to anyone who is not a party position. Each party position has full read of the joint record, write on its own unilateral acts, and no unilateral write on joint facts, which require joint evidence.
exceptions: Adjudication access: a court or arbitral tribunal obtains the record once a dispute is escalated under the agreed forum clause
Regulatory or tax authority access on a stated legal basis, with the parties notified unless notification is prohibited
Auditor, financier or prospective assignee due diligence under a time-limited grant, normally on a redacted projection
Statutory disclosure duties, including unfair-term and data-sharing controls, that override a confidentiality clause
Emergency continuity access by a designated custodian where a party's system is unavailable, logged and reviewed afterwards
Adjudication access after a dispute is escalated to the contractual forum
Consented counterparty-status disclosure of existence and coarse performance standing to credit or rating consumers
Public-summary projection of existence, parties and subject-matter class where a transparency register is agreed or required
Mandatory regulatory disclosure that is an overriding mandatory rule of the forum
audit_requirements: Log every read of a restricted finding or artifact with requester, purpose, grant reference and timestamp carrying an explicit offset
Log grant issuance, scope, expiry and revocation as first-class events
Keep the audit log append-only and tamper-evident, with each segment chained to the digest of its predecessor
Retain audit entries at least as long as the record element they describe, and never dispose of them earlier

Log execution, amendment, performance acceptance, breach declaration, avoidance, assignment and every access exception with actor, artifact, event time and ingestion time in RFC 3339 with seconds and an explicit offset or Z
Preserve content hashes of each expression so that later projections can be verified
Record who opened adjudication access and under which dispute-clause identifier

required_fields: Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL
read_order: Read AGENTS.md first to learn the model name, entry kind and the four resolution URLs
Follow the Specification URL to load the bundle, layer, finding and question structure and the identity and timestamp rules
Follow the Storage type URL to learn the concrete projection in use, whether documents, rows, graph nodes or files, and its canonicalisation rules
Follow the Interface URL to learn the read, create, update and delete operations available and their scopes
Follow the Processes URL for formation, performance, amendment, notice, dispute and disposition procedures
Read the Projection Catalogue URL before emitting anything to a non-party, and the Governing Law and Forum Declaration URL before asserting any legal consequence

coverage.claim: Base claude structure, plus two grok findings, covers agreement identity and legal frame, party positions and authority, formation and execution, agreed text and commercial terms, the obligation/performance/variance lifecycle, and record governance for business-to-business commercial agreements as grounded in the cited instruments. Coverage is asserted only for the sourced instruments and the profiles actually tested; it is not a universal or complete account of commercial contracting, national validity law, or any sector profile, and no conformance to any cited standard is claimed without test evidence.

checklist.notes: Agreement identity, instance boundary and expression addressing are a dedicated finding; party identity uses a governed global identifier; the identity priority places the authoritative master-system identifier first and excludes dates as identifiers.

Formation, execution, conditional effectiveness, due and performed obligations, breach, remedy, amendment, transfer, termination and post-termination survival each have findings, following the CISG and UNIDROIT division of the contractual life.

Party positions to entities, obligations to source clauses, milestones to obligations, performance to obligations, remedies to breaches and constituent documents to precedence ranks are all modelled; sibling model links are declared as composition.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset is mandated; conclusion, dispatch, deemed receipt, execution, effectiveness, due, cure, performance, amendment, termination and disposition times are distinct, with event time separated from observation time.
A dedicated finding applies an agent, activity and derivation vocabulary to every assertion, and derived artifacts such as obligation rule sets carry traceability to source clause identifiers.
Joint ownership by the party positions is a policy and a question; joint facts versus unilateral acts are distinguished, and stewardship and access-grant models are referenced rather than duplicated.

Definiteness of the offer, form requirements, authority verification, signature validation, integrity verification and unfair-term screening are separate validation questions with recorded outcomes and observation times.
Deny-by-default for non-parties, four grant scopes, projection-based disclosure, redaction rules and five enumerated exceptions including adjudication and regulatory access.
Retention triggers, limitation periods, legal holds, the erasure-versus-preservation conflict, redaction in place with preserved digests and evidenced disposition are all modelled.

Alignments are declared with claim levels and mapping conflicts recorded; projections to non-parties are governed artifacts with published omission lists; the model is expressed independently of any storage format.
Subject-matter class, uniform-regime applicability, clause class, party role, notice kind, remedy kind and trade term are all coded against named schemes with versions.
Signing authority basis, limits, verification and the consequences of excess are a dedicated finding, with consent authority for transfers handled separately.
Performance metrics with values, units and thresholds, and quantification of claimed loss against caps or liquidated sums, are explicit questions.
Place of business, named place for the trade term, place of risk transfer, arbitral seat and the offset of the place of execution are captured; geospatial geometry is not required for this model.
Signature assurance, digest fixity, tamper-evident chained audit segments and confidentiality scope are modelled; cryptographic key management is delegated to the trust-service domain.
Authority excess, validity defects, excuse for impediment and hardship, compelled disclosure and erasure conflicts are each modelled as explicit exception paths rather than error states.

known_omissions: Consumer and employment contracts are excluded, so unfair-term regimes specific to consumers are not modelled.
Statutory late-payment interest defaults were not grounded in a verified primary source in this pass; the model carries an interest-basis element but no jurisdictional default table.
Sector-specific master agreement lifecycles, such as derivatives event models, are treated as EXTEND candidates and are not detailed.
Tax determination, customs classification and transfer pricing are out of scope even though they depend on the trade term and price elements.
Escrow, retention of title and security interests are referenced only at their boundary with property transfer, which the uniform sales regime excludes.
Smart-contract execution semantics on distributed ledgers are referenced through the data-sharing essential-requirements source but not modelled as an execution substrate.
Automated clause extraction quality metrics are represented only as a provenance confidence field, with no scoring scheme specified.
Multi-tier supply chain flow-down of terms to subcontracts is acknowledged in the third-party finding but not modelled as a propagation mechanism.
National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, unconscionability, illegality, consideration in common law) lack a uniform primary schema because CISG Article 4 excludes validity.

UCC Article 2 battle of forms (§ 2-207), adequate assurance (§ 2-609) and remedy catalogue were not fetched as live primary text beyond § 2-201; they are regional competitors to CISG, not canonical nodes.

UNIDROIT hardship, set-off, plurality of obligors, assignment chapters and limitation Chapter 10 are aligned from the 2016 instrument as a whole; individual articles beyond formation Chapter 2 were not re-fetched in this run.
The 1974 Limitation Convention (as amended 1980) is a related sales time-bar treaty and is not modelled as a first-class bundle.
Industry standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and clickwrap or platform terms of service are profiles, not core findings.
Smart-contract bytecode, oracles and on-chain settlement have only UNIDROIT automated-contracting comment support and remain an evidence gap.
Supervening sanctions, export controls and COVID-era hardship practice are public-law or factual overlays without a dedicated primary contract schema here.
eIDAS qualified-signature levels and UETA state enactments were not fetched; MLES is the cross-border alignment used instead.
PECL and the Draft Common Frame of Reference were not fetched live and are not treated as canonical.
Data-processing addenda, ESG clauses and modern slavery warranties are emerging clause classes without a governing primary standard in the source set.
conflicts: The uniform sales regime frees contracts of writing and proof requirements, while the New York Convention requires an arbitration agreement in writing: a contract may be validly formed orally yet carry an unenforceable arbitration clause. The model therefore records the writing evidence for the forum clause separately from the formation evidence.

Statutory and contractual retention duties conflict with personal-data erasure rights. The model resolves this by redaction in place with preserved digests, which is a defensible reconciliation rather than a settled legal rule.

Expression-level clause identifiers change when a provision is renumbered by amendment, while work-level identifiers persist. Consumers that key on expression identifiers will break across amendments; the model requires both to be stored.

Hardship and renegotiation exist in the UNIDROIT Principles but have no counterpart in the uniform sales regime, so excuse semantics differ by governing law; the excuse ground code must be interpreted against the declared governing law.
Trade terms allocate cost and risk but not property, and the uniform sales regime expressly excludes the passing of property, so title must be sourced from national law outside this model.
Regional qualified-signature presumptions are not globally comparable with technology-neutral reliability tests, so a single signature assurance level cannot be treated as universally probative.
CISG Article 11 (no writing required) conflicts with UCC § 2-201 (signed writing for $500+) and with CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations that restore a writing rule the parties cannot derogate from.

CISG Article 16 makes offers generally revocable until acceptance is dispatched, with reliance and stated irrevocability exceptions; many civil-law systems treat a fixed-time offer as irrevocable. UNIDROIT Article 2.1.4 comment records this as historically irreconcilable and selects CISG's main rule.

CISG Article 19 material-alteration list is more rigid than UNIDROIT Article 2.1.11 comment, which makes materiality contextual; UCC § 2-207 (unfetched beyond awareness) is a third battle-of-forms regime.
CISG Article 28 lets a court refuse specific performance according to its own law; civil-law systems more readily order performance.
CISG Article 79 impediment is not UNIDROIT hardship; treating force majeure certificates as automatic exemption would be a false conformance claim.
HCCH Article 3 choice of non-State rules of law is commonly allowed in arbitration and often disallowed in State courts unless forum law says otherwise.

Agreed penalties may be unenforceable as penalties in some common-law systems while liquidated damages and civil-law contractual penalties are treated differently; LegalRuleML Penalty is a deontic link, not a guarantee of enforceability.

Akoma Ntoso is designed primarily for parliamentary, legislative and judicial documents; using it for private commercial contracts is an alignment of document mechanics, not a claim that Akoma Ntoso normatively governs private agreements.
regional_assumptions: Electronic signature and trust-service assurance levels and the essential requirements for data-sharing smart contracts are drawn from European Union instruments and are regional alignments, not universal rules.
The Hague choice-of-law principles are non-binding soft law whose adoption varies by jurisdiction; the express-or-tacit choice model may not match a given forum's conflict rules.

The uniform sales regime applies only where the parties' places of business are in contracting states or conflict rules lead there, and it may be excluded by agreement, so its applicability is recorded as a declaration rather than assumed.

Common-law consideration and privity doctrines and civil-law cause requirements differ from the restatement-style formation model used here; formation validity must be re-tested under the declared governing law.
Limitation periods, notice-deeming rules and permitted electronic execution formalities vary by jurisdiction and are treated as configuration rather than as model constants.
International sales between CISG Contracting States default to CISG unless excluded; purely domestic US goods sales more often meet UCC Article 2, including the § 2-201 writing rule.
Rome I Regulation choice-of-law mechanics in the EU were not fetched; HCCH Principles are used as the cross-border alignment and expressly sit alongside Rome I as a non-binding guide.
Article 96 writing reservations (for example historically relevant for some CISG Contracting States) must be checked per party place of business rather than assumed absent.
Islamic finance, OHADA uniform acts and PRC Contract/Civil Code particularities are not included and would be regional extensions.
Places of business, not nationality, determine CISG internationality (CISG Articles 1(3) and 10).
The default operating picture is a B2B commercial agreement, including but not limited to international sales, rather than a consumer, employment or purely domestic consumer-protection regime.
Party-mirror joint ownership is the stewardship default: each party holds a full record and joint facts change only by joint events.
Where CISG and a domestic writing statute both claim to apply, the model records both rules and the Article 96 reservation state rather than silently preferring one.
Event time and observation or ingestion time are stored separately whenever a notice, acceptance or breach declaration is transmitted rather than contemporaneously logged.
Alignment to a standard is not a conformance claim for any particular agreement instance.
adversarial_checks: Tested against oral and conduct-formed contracts: identity must not be derived from a document digest, since no executed document may exist. Agreement identity is therefore separated from expression identity and from execution evidence.

Tested against framework agreements with call-offs: the instance boundary question asks whether obligations arise directly or only on call-off, which prevents a single record silently conflating a master agreement with each purchase under it.

Tested against the battle of forms: the governing text may be a composite of two competing form sets, so incorporation and precedence are modelled independently of the signed instrument rather than assumed from it.
Rejected the framing of a contract as an organization, upholding the registry validation flag: party positions reference organization records, and no organizational attributes are carried here.
Rejected a standalone signature bundle: signature is evidence supporting execution and has no independent decision surface, so it is a finding within formation rather than a top-level concern.

Rejected modelling dispute proceedings, awards and enforcement inline: no cited primary source supports duplicating adjudication process in the contract record, so only the clause, the writing evidence and the escalation state remain in scope.
Rejected owning executed prices as price observations: the valuation model reads a projection, which prevents a confidentiality leak becoming a structural dependency.
Tested whether milestones deserve artifacts: any published schedule can diverge from the clauses that generate it, so schedules are declared derived projections rather than authoritative artifacts.
The registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization is honoured: party positions bind actors; the agreement is a joint record, not an O1 entity.
CISG was not generalised to services, consumer sales, validity or property; those exclusions are modelled as out-of-scope or sibling boundaries.
UNIDROIT PICC were not treated as automatically binding; they apply when chosen, used to interpret or supplement, or selected as HCCH Article 3 rules of law.
Choice of court and arbitration clauses are stored as terms and then handed to the dispute-resolution sibling; HCCH Principles' exclusion of those agreements from choice-of-law scope is respected.
A date is never used as an identifier; execution date is a temporal attribute beside master-system id, IRI and UUID or ULID.
Electronic signature reliability is aligned to MLES rather than inventing a vendor-specific PKI as the semantic model.
Public-summary and credit-standing projections were checked so they cannot leak clause text, prices or personal signatory data by default.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently reached entry_kind=aggregate and both explicitly uphold the registry validation flag that a contract is not an organization. The boundary is the jointly owned multi-party agreement record composed of party positions, clause structure, deontic obligations and lifecycle events, with the legal entities, the procurement award process, adjudication proceedings, proprietary/title effects, insolvency and settlement execution held as neighbouring models. Claude's six sourced boundary notes and grok's CISG/HCCH sphere-of-application notes agree on every exclusion, so the boundary is settled before any node is accepted.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Claude has six sourced boundary notes naming concrete neighbour models, an explicit inline_only_rationale for every finding that mints no artifact, a sixteen-dimension coverage checklist with no self-declared gap, and separate findings for provenance, access, retention and interoperability. Grok is stronger on CISG article-level depth but declares a validation gap and lumps notices, dispute clauses, joint record, access and retention into one composite finding, which is the less clear boundary.

decisions.concept: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
decisions.rationale: A genuine hole in the base: the agreed text can be addressed and ranked but not construed. CISG Articles 7-9 give it primary-source grounding and it duplicates nothing already present.

decisions.concept: Anticipatory breach, suspension, adequate assurance, Nachfrist
decisions.rationale: The base jumps from breach declaration to remedy election with no additional-period, suspension or assurance path. CISG Articles 47, 63, 71-73 support four distinct states the base cannot currently represent.

decisions.concept: Writing requirement, statute of frauds and Article 96 reservations
decisions.disposition: rejected as duplicative; deferred as question-level enrichment
decisions.rationale: The base finding execution-signature-and-form already owns the form-requirement decision surface. Adding grok's finding would create a second execution node overlapping on signature method. The CISG Article 11 versus UCC 2-201 versus Article 12/96 tension is recorded as a publication hold and deferred research item instead of new structure.

decisions.concept: Remedy catalogue detail (mitigation, substitute-transaction measure, Article 28 forum filter, restitution)
decisions.rationale: Base breach-excuse-and-remedy already carries remedy election and quantification against caps or liquidated sums, and termination-expiry-and-survival carries wind-down and final accounting. Grok's additions are measurement refinements inside an existing surface, not a missing surface.

decisions.concept: Composite notices/dispute-clause/joint-record/access/retention finding
decisions.disposition: rejected in favour of base decomposition
decisions.rationale: The base already separates notice-and-formal-communication, dispute-forum-and-enforceability, access-and-disclosure-control, retention-limitation-and-deletion and provenance-and-audit-trail. Importing a composite would blur four distinct governance decision surfaces the base keeps apart.

decisions.concept: Assignment, guarantees and third-party rights as one node
decisions.rationale: The base splits this correctly into third-party-positions (agents, guarantors, beneficiaries, subcontracting) and assignment-and-novation (transfer kind, consent, change of control, position continuity). Grok's single node would double-own both.

decisions.concept: Clause isomorphism and standard-versus-negotiated flag
decisions.rationale: Base cla-q-machine-rule-link covers the rule-to-provision assertion and oac-q-standard-terms covers incorporation of competing form sets. Many-to-many isomorphism is a refinement of an existing question, not a new finding.

decisions.concept: Delivery, conformity, examination and seller cure
decisions.rationale: Base delivery-and-risk-transfer holds conformity and examination periods, performance-record-and-acceptance holds acceptance and rejection states, and milestone-and-due-condition holds cure periods. Grok's node restates all three.

decisions.concept: Risk passing, impediment and hardship
decisions.rationale: Base del-q-risk-transfer covers the passing of risk and brm-q-excuse-ground covers impediment and hardship with evidence. CISG Article 80 self-caused failure is a worthwhile question-level addition but does not justify a parallel finding.

decisions.concept: Statutory default duties not created by a clause (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59)
decisions.rationale: Base obl-q-source-clause presumes a provision creates each duty, so gap-filled statutory duties currently have no source. This is a real modelling question about whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, and it needs its own resolution rather than an imported node.

decisions.concept: Artifact discipline via inline_only_rationale
decisions.rationale: The base refuses to mint artifacts for derived readings of clause text (payment terms, protective terms, milestones, termination state) to prevent a second normatively significant copy of the executed wording. This discipline is preserved and grok's flatter artifact set is not merged.

decisions.concept: Incoterms trade terms and risk-transfer point
decisions.rationale: Grok has no trade-term source at all; the base grounds delivery, cost allocation and the named place in ICC Incoterms 2020, which is required for any goods-sale profile.

decisions.concept: eIDAS and Data Act sourced elements
decisions.rationale: Signature assurance levels, trust-service concepts and unfair-term controls in the base come from EU instruments. They stay, marked as regional alignment rather than universal rule, consistent with grok's use of the UNCITRAL model laws as the cross-border baseline.

decisions.concept: National validity doctrines (mistake, fraud, duress, illegality)
decisions.rationale: CISG Article 4 excludes validity and both providers place it in a sibling or overlay. The base keeps only the assertion surface in effectiveness-conditions-and-validity, which is the correct minimum without importing grok's declared validation gap.

publicationHolds: Source verification hold: none of the 16 base URLs or the 5 grok-only URLs were re-fetched in this adjudication. Every accepted source must be resolved live and version-pinned before publication, with particular attention to the two different LegalRuleML OS URLs, Akoma Ntoso naming-convention v1.0 versus core v1.0 Part 1, UBL 2.4 Committee Specification status, Incoterms 2020, and eIDAS 'as amended by the European Digital Identity framework'.

Multi-profile validation hold: the merged structure must be exercised against at least three domain profiles before publication - an international CISG sale of goods, a domestic US goods sale where UCC Article 2 and the section 2-201 writing rule apply, and a services or framework-plus-call-off agreement where no goods and no executed single instrument exist.

Writing-rule hold: CISG Article 11 (no writing required), CISG Articles 12 and 96 reservations, and UCC section 2-201 must be carried as co-recorded competing rules with the reservation state per party place of business. Do not publish a single resolved writing rule.

Regional-labelling hold: eIDAS signature assurance levels and the Data Act unfair-term and smart-contract essential-requirement material are EU-regional and must be published as regional alignments, not universal rules, alongside the technology-neutral UNCITRAL reliability test.

No-conformance hold: alignments to UBL, LegalRuleML, Akoma Ntoso, PROV-O and RFC 3339 are declared alignments only. Publication must state the claim level and must not assert tested conformance for any instance without test evidence.
deferredResearch: Fetch UCC Article 2 primary text beyond section 2-201 - specifically 2-207 battle of forms, 2-609 adequate assurance, and the 2-706/2-708/2-712/2-713 damages measures - to test whether the accepted anticipatory-breach finding holds under a second, non-CISG regime.

Resolve whether an obligation's source may be a legal norm rather than a clause, so that gap-filled statutory duties (CISG Articles 30, 53, 31, 55, 57-59) can be instantiated without a fabricated provision reference.
Ground statutory late-payment interest defaults in a verified primary source, or publish the interest-basis element explicitly as configuration with no jurisdictional default table.
Assess the 1974 UN Limitation Convention as amended in 1980 as a distinct time-bar instrument against the base retention and limitation-period questions.
Evaluate sector standard forms (ISDA Master, FIDIC, GAFTA, BIMCO) and insurance policies as EXTEND profiles, and confirm the base carries the extension points those profiles would need.

Compare eIDAS qualified-signature presumptions, UETA/ESIGN state enactments and the UNCITRAL Model Law on Electronic Signatures reliability test to determine whether a single cross-regional signature assurance scale is defensible.

Decide whether set-off, plurality of obligors and transfer of obligations (UNIDROIT Chapters 8, 9, 11) belong in the accepted transfer surface or in a sibling model, since neither provider currently owns set-off.
Specify the smart-contract execution substrate boundary: whether self-executing performance is evidence of performance only, or requires its own recorded execution state.

bundles.name: Identity and Legal Frame
bundles.description: What this agreement is, how it is uniquely denoted, what kind of transaction it governs and which law and forum apply to it.
bundles.rationale: Before any term can be read or any obligation operated, an agent must fix the record's identity boundary and the legal regime that determines validity, interpretation, performance and remedies; the HCCH Principles make the chosen law govern exactly those matters.

layers.name: Agreement Identity and Classification
layers.description: Denotation of the agreement instance and the coded classification that selects the applicable regime and term expectations.

findings.name: Agreement Record Identity and Instance Boundary
findings.description: How one agreement is distinguished from another, which identifier is authoritative, and where a framework agreement ends and a call-off begins.

findings.name: Subject-Matter Classification and Applicable Regime
findings.description: Coded classification of what the agreement does, and the declared applicability or exclusion of regimes such as the CISG.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Classification is coded reference data asserted on the agreement record and resolved against external code lists; it produces no separate document. The evidence for a regime exclusion is the clause artifact already held by the clause-addressability finding, so duplicating an artifact here would fragment the executed text.

layers.name: Applicable Law and Dispute Forum
layers.description: The chosen governing law, the mandatory rules it cannot displace, and the forum agreed for disputes together with the form evidence that forum requires.

findings.name: Governing Law and Mandatory Rules
findings.description: Which law the parties chose, whether expressly or tacitly, the severability of that choice, and the overriding rules that apply regardless.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The governing-law declaration is an attribute of the agreement plus a pointer into the executed clause tree; the clause text itself is the artifact of the clause-addressability finding. Minting a separate artifact would create a second, divergent copy of a normative provision.

findings.name: Dispute Forum, Escalation and Written-Form Evidence
findings.description: The agreed forum, escalation ladder and seat, plus the writing evidence an arbitration agreement needs to be enforceable across borders.

bundles.name: Parties, Identity and Authority
bundles.description: Who is bound, in what role, on whose behalf, and with what verified power to bind.
bundles.rationale: A contract binds legal persons through positions filled by representatives; UNIDROIT treats authority of agents as a distinct chapter and the LEI provides a governed identifier, so party position, party identity and signing authority are separable decision surfaces.

layers.name: Party Positions and Legal Identification
layers.description: The roles the agreement creates and the verified real-world entities that occupy them.

findings.name: Party Position and Contractual Role
findings.description: The abstract positions the agreement creates, their roles, and how liability is shared where several parties occupy one side.
findings.inline_only_rationale: A party position is a structural slot in the agreement record, not a document. Its evidence is the executed text and the identity verification record held by the neighbouring finding; creating an artifact for a slot would assert a document that does not exist.

findings.name: Legal Identification and Place of Business
findings.description: The governed identifier for each party, the verification evidence behind it, and the place of business that drives regime applicability.

layers.name: Authority and Representation
layers.description: The power of the individuals and intermediaries who bind the parties, and the positions of third parties who are affected without signing.

findings.name: Signing Authority and Capacity
findings.description: Who executed the agreement for each party, on what basis they were empowered, and what limits bounded that power.

findings.name: Agents, Guarantors and Third-Party Beneficiaries
findings.description: Positions held by parties who act for, secure or benefit from the agreement without being principal obligors.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Third-party positions are structural relations derived from the executed clauses; where a guarantee or agency is itself a separate agreement, it is a distinct instance of this model rather than an artifact of this finding, which avoids double-owning another contract's text.

bundles.name: Formation, Execution and Effectiveness
bundles.description: How the agreement came into existence, how consent was expressed and evidenced, and when it began to bite.
bundles.rationale: The CISG devotes a whole Part to formation by offer and acceptance, the UN electronic communications convention governs dispatch and receipt of the messages that carry consent, and eIDAS and the UNCITRAL Model Law govern the evidentiary weight of the resulting signature.

layers.name: Consent and Conclusion
layers.description: The offer, acceptance or conduct that concluded the agreement, and whose standard terms became part of it.

findings.name: Offer, Acceptance and Incorporated Standard Terms
findings.description: The communications and conduct that concluded the contract, when and where they took effect, and which standard terms were incorporated when both sides sent their own.

layers.name: Execution and Effectiveness
layers.description: The signature or seal evidence attached to the agreed text, and the conditions that had to be met before it took effect.

findings.name: Execution, Signature Type and Form Requirement
findings.description: How the agreement was signed or sealed, the assurance level and validation evidence of that signature, and any form requirement it had to satisfy.

findings.name: Conditions Precedent, Effectiveness and Validity Defects
findings.description: The gap between execution and effect: conditions to be satisfied, approvals to be obtained, and defects that can unwind consent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Effectiveness is a computed state over conditions, clauses and events already held elsewhere; the documents that satisfy a condition (a regulatory approval, a guarantee) are artifacts owned by their own models or by the notice finding. Creating an artifact here would duplicate them.

bundles.name: Agreed Text and Commercial Terms
bundles.description: The structure of the agreed text, the documents that make it up, and the substantive commercial and protective terms it contains.
bundles.rationale: Operating a contract requires addressing individual provisions stably across amendments, knowing which documents govern when they conflict, and reading the price, delivery and protective terms as structured values rather than prose.

layers.name: Document Structure and Precedence
layers.description: How provisions are addressed, which documents constitute the contract, how conflicts between them resolve, and which language governs.

findings.name: Clause Addressability and Structure
findings.description: Stable identification of individual provisions across versions, their classification and their machine-readable form.

findings.name: Constituent Documents, Precedence and Authentic Language
findings.description: Which documents together form the contract, how conflicts between them are ranked, and which language version controls.

findings.name: Interpretation, usages and subsequent conduct
findings.description: CISG Article 8 interprets statements and conduct first by a party's intent where the other party knew or could not have been unaware of it, otherwise by a reasonable person of the same kind in the same circumstances, having regard to negotiations, practices, usages and subsequent conduct. Article 9 binds parties to agreed usages and established practices and, unless otherwise agreed, to international trade usages they knew or ought to have known. Article 7 requires interpretation of the Convention itself with regard to international character, uniformity and good faith. UNIDROIT Chapter 4 (as part of PICC 2016) supplies complementary interpretation and gap-filling. These materials are evidence for meaning, not a second contract.

layers.name: Commercial and Protective Terms
layers.description: Price and payment, delivery and risk, and the warranty, liability, confidentiality and compliance terms that allocate exposure.

findings.name: Price, Consideration and Payment Terms
findings.description: How the price is fixed or determined, in what currency, when payment falls due and what follows late payment.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Payment terms are structured values derived from clauses; the payment schedule itself is held by the milestone finding and the resulting invoices belong to a settlement model. Asserting a separate artifact here would either duplicate the clause text or claim ownership of financial documents outside this model's boundary.

findings.name: Delivery Terms, Risk Transfer and Conformity
findings.description: The trade term governing delivery and cost allocation, the point at which risk passes, and the conformity and inspection regime.

findings.name: Warranty, Liability, Confidentiality and Compliance Terms
findings.description: Terms that allocate risk and constrain conduct: warranties, liability caps and exclusions, indemnities, confidentiality, intellectual property, data protection and fairness controls.
findings.inline_only_rationale: These are structured readings of clauses already carried by the clause tree artifact. Holding them as separate artifacts would create a normatively significant second copy of contract wording whose divergence from the executed text could not be detected.

bundles.name: Obligations, Performance and Variance
bundles.description: What the agreement requires, when it falls due, what actually happened, and how the parties change or end it.
bundles.rationale: The uniform sales regime and the UNIDROIT Principles both organise the operative life of a contract around obligations, performance, non-performance, excuse and remedy; LegalRuleML supplies the machine-readable deontic form of those duties.

layers.name: Obligations and Schedule
layers.description: The duties the agreement creates and the temporal conditions that make them performable or overdue.

findings.name: Obligation as Deontic Specification
findings.description: Each duty expressed with its deontic type, bearer, auxiliary party, source clause and the violation and reparation that follow non-compliance.

findings.name: Milestones, Due Conditions and Cure Periods
findings.description: The calendar and event conditions that make a duty performable or overdue, together with grace and cure periods.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Milestones are computed projections over obligations, dates and events. Any published schedule is a projection artifact governed by the interoperability finding; a standalone schedule artifact here would risk becoming an authoritative timetable that diverges from the clauses that generate it.

layers.name: Performance and Non-Performance
layers.description: What was rendered and accepted, and what happens when performance fails, is excused or triggers a remedy.

findings.name: Performance Record, Measurement and Acceptance
findings.description: Evidence that a duty was performed, the measured result against agreed criteria, and the counterparty's acceptance or rejection.

findings.name: Non-Performance, Excuse and Remedy
findings.description: Declared failure to perform, its severity, any excuse such as impediment or hardship, and the remedy elected or agreed.

findings.name: Breach, additional time, cure, suspension and anticipatory breach
findings.description: CISG Article 25 defines fundamental breach as detriment that substantially deprives the other party of what it is entitled to expect, unless the result was not foreseeable. Articles 47 and 63 allow a Nachfrist additional period of reasonable length; during it the fixing party may not resort to inconsistent remedies but keeps damages for delay. Articles 71–72 allow suspension for apparent future non-performance of a substantial part, with immediate notice and a duty to continue if adequate assurance is provided, and avoidance for clear future fundamental breach. Article 73 deals with instalments. LegalRuleML Violation, Suborder, Penalty and Reparation model the deontic consequence of breach. A breach declaration is a party event, not a court judgment; adjudication is a sibling process.

layers.name: Change, Communication and Closure
layers.description: Amendment of the terms, transfer of positions, the formal notices that operate the contract, and the way it ends.

findings.name: Amendment and Variation
findings.description: Agreed changes to the terms, the formality they require, the clauses they touch and the version they produce.

findings.name: Assignment, Novation and Change of Control
findings.description: Transfer of rights or of a whole position to a successor, the consent it requires, and its effect on the record's continuity.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Where the transfer is documented, that document is an executed amendment or a separate agreement instance and is already covered by those findings. Recording a duplicate artifact here would create two independent chains of title over the same position.

findings.name: Notices and Formal Communication
findings.description: The formal messages that operate the contract, the channels and addresses they must use, and the rules that deem them received.

findings.name: Termination, Expiry and Survival
findings.description: How the agreement ends, on what ground, which provisions survive and what wind-down obligations remain.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Termination is effected by a notice, an expiry of term, or an amendment-like release, all of which are already held as artifacts by the notice and amendment findings. The end state itself is a derived status over those events plus the clause tree.

bundles.name: Record Governance, Evidence and Interoperability
bundles.description: How the jointly owned record stays trustworthy, who may see what, how long it is kept, and how it is exchanged without leaking terms.
bundles.rationale: Records management standards make authenticity, reliability, integrity and usability the defining properties of a record and require metadata and disposition control; provenance vocabulary and interchange standards make those properties expressible across systems.

layers.name: Provenance and Integrity
layers.description: Attribution of every assertion in the record and cryptographic fixity of the executed text.

findings.name: Provenance, Attribution and Text Integrity
findings.description: Who or what generated each assertion, from which source it was derived, when, and what digest and signature evidence fixes the executed text against later alteration.

layers.name: Access, Retention and Exchange
layers.description: Confidentiality of the joint record, its disposition over time, and the projections through which it interoperates.

findings.name: Access, Disclosure and Redaction
findings.description: Who may read which part of the joint record, under what grant and purpose, and how compelled disclosure is handled.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Access grants are governed records owned by the access-grant model and referenced here; the evidence of each access is an entry in the provenance and audit log artifact. A separate artifact would fork authority over grants away from their owning model.

findings.name: Retention, Limitation Periods and Disposition
findings.description: How long the record must be kept, what suspends deletion, and how authorised disposition is carried out and evidenced.

findings.name: External Alignment and Projections
findings.description: Declared alignments to external vocabularies and the reduced views published to non-parties, with what each view omits.

model.name: Decision / Rationale
model.purpose: Govern the decision as an inspectable knowledge object: the issue to be resolved, the objectives and constraints that frame it, the alternatives considered, the criteria and evaluation applied, the selected outcome and its disposition, together with the rationale, evidence citations, authority, lifecycle, provenance and access governance that let a machine agent understand, reconstruct and reuse the choice.
model.scope_statement: WM-KNW-010 governs the content of a decision taken on a specific occasion and the reasoning offered for it, independently of storage format and access interface. It covers stable decision identity and version discrimination; decision type and jurisdictional profile; the decision question, objectives, context and affected subjects; constraints and the decision rules relied upon; the candidate alternative set including any required no-action baseline; eligibility screening and recorded exclusion; criteria, measures, scales and weights; evaluation results, comparison and sensitivity; the selected alternative, disposition, explicit outcome statement, attached conditions and stated consequences; the rationale and argument structure that justify the outcome together with citations to evidence; the participants, roles and authority basis under which the decision was taken; and the lifecycle, provenance, access, retention and quality governance of decision content. It does not govern the activity that produced the decision, the document that carries it, the legal instrument that may enact it, the evidence items it cites, any executable rule or decision service, or downstream implementation.
in_scope: Stable decision identity, version discriminator and supersession links between decisions
Decision type, jurisdictional profile binding and profile-required content elements
The decision question, its admissible answer space and the problem or issue that triggered it
Objectives, critical success factors and expected effects on declared indicators
Decision context, dependencies on input data and upstream decisions, and affected subjects
Binding constraints, admissibility conditions and the decision rules relied upon, stated declaratively
The registered candidate alternative set, including a no-action or business-as-usual baseline where a profile requires one
Eligibility screening and recorded reasons for excluding alternatives from detailed evaluation
Evaluation criteria, measures, scales, preference directions and weighting schemes
Recorded evaluation results, aggregation, ranking and sensitivity findings
The selected alternative, disposition, explicit outcome statement, effect onset and applicability
Conditions, reservations, accepted risks, stated consequences and follow-on decisions
Rationale, argument structure and explanation linking the outcome to objectives, criteria and cited evidence
Participants, roles, delegation and the authority basis on which the decision was taken
Decision-content lifecycle states, revision history, provenance, access classification, retention and quality governance
out_of_scope: The decision-making or approval activity itself, including convening, deliberation, voting and approval execution (WM-ACT-024)
The document or record container that renders, files, publishes or preserves the decision (WM-REC-010)
The legal judgment as a binding legal instrument, its enforceability and its citation regime (WM-POL-021)
Generic claim assertion, truth-value and claim-conflict machinery (WM-KNW-007)
Evidence items themselves, their appraisal, integrity and chain of custody (WM-KNW-008)
Executable rules, policies, decision services and rule engines, and their runtime evaluation or enforcement
Audit-trail records produced by an external audit or logging service
Implementation, delivery and change execution that follows a decision (WM-ACT-032)
Domain-specific decision rule content such as clinical protocols, credit scorecards, procurement award formulas or sentencing guidelines
Mathematical decision-analysis method definitions such as utility theory, AHP, ELECTRE or PROMETHEE, which bind only as optional external methods

boundary_notes.distinction: This model governs decision content. DMN's Decision element only points at decisionMaker, decisionOwner, usingProcess and usingTask by reference, and ISO/IEC/IEEE 15288 places decision management as a process. Convening, deliberation, voting and approval execution therefore belong to the activity model and are referenced, never reproduced here.

Akoma Ntoso separates the abstract Work and its Expression from the Manifestation and Item that carry it. Decision content is the governed subject here; rendering, filing, formatting, publication and preservation of the carrying record belong to the record model.

A judgment is a legal instrument with binding force, its own citation regime and a judgmentBody whose introduction, background, motivation and decision sections are editorially structured. This model captures the decision content a judgment may express, not the instrument's legal effect.

A claim asserts that something is the case. A decision selects among registered alternatives and produces a disposition. Generic assertion identity, truth-value and claim-conflict machinery stay with the parent model; only decision-specific specialisation is modelled here.

Cited evidence is bound by identifier with a stated role in an evaluation result. Evidence appraisal, integrity, sufficiency and chain of custody remain with the evidence model; NASA's guidance on assumptions and their supporting evidence is used only to justify the citation binding.

boundary_notes.neighbor: Executable rule, policy or decision service
boundary_notes.distinction: DMN decision logic, business knowledge models and decision tables are executable artefacts deployed and run by a decision service. This model records the rules relied upon, their declared hit policy and a versioned reference to the source rule, and never owns runtime evaluation, enforcement or the engine's execution trace.

A change request may be resolved by a decision; the decision carries a back-reference to the resolved issue. The request's own lifecycle, prioritisation and the implementation of the change belong to that model, as does the monitoring and compliance work that a record of decision may direct.

boundary_notes.neighbor: WM-KNW-010 rationale, participation and governance areas (same model)
boundary_notes.distinction: Argument structure, explanation, participants and authority basis, and the lifecycle, provenance, access, retention and audit governance of decision content are governed by the other areas of this same model. The decision-core structures supply their subject matter by reference and do not restate them.

functions.name: Frame the decision
functions.description: Establish the governed decision record: mint or bind its identifier, classify it against a decision type and jurisdictional profile, state the decision question and admissible answer space, record the triggering issue, objectives and critical success factors, and declare context dependencies and binding constraints.
inputs: Decision type code and jurisdictional profile identifier
Decision question text and admissible answer space
Objectives, critical success factors and impacted indicator references
Declared constraints, required input references and upstream decision references
outputs: Framed decision record carrying a resolvable identifier and version discriminator
Recorded decision question with its admissible answer space
Derived list of profile-required content elements
preconditions: An identifier is available from the identity priority order, master-system identifier first
The decision type and its bound profile are published by the profile custodian
effects: A uniquely identified decision record exists and is resolvable
Profile-required content elements are declared so later completeness checks are decidable
Framing content becomes the fixed reference against which the outcome statement is validated

functions.name: Register a candidate alternative
functions.description: Add a candidate alternative to the decision's alternative set with its own identifier, kind code and description, including registration of a no-action or business-as-usual baseline where the bound profile requires one.
inputs: Alternative kind code, including baseline or do-minimum where applicable
Variant-of reference where the alternative varies another
outputs: Registered alternative with its own identifier and registration ordinal
Updated alternative set for the decision
Baseline presence indicator for the bound profile
preconditions: The decision has been framed and its profile binding is known
The alternative is described in terms that the declared criteria can be applied to
effects: The alternative set is extended append-only; registered alternatives are never silently removed
Absence of a profile-required baseline becomes a detectable validation failure
Variants remain distinguishable from independently registered alternatives

functions.name: Declare the evaluation criteria and weights
functions.description: Record the criteria against which alternatives will be compared, each with its measure, scale, unit and preference direction, the separation of mandatory pass-or-fail criteria from compensatory ones, and the weighting scheme with its declared method or an explicit statement that no weighting is used.
inputs: Objectives and critical success factors from the framed decision
Candidate criteria with measures, scales and preference directions
Weighting method identifier and weight values where a weighting scheme applies
Monetisation convention where a criterion is expressed in monetary terms
outputs: Declared criterion set addressable by criterion identifier
Declared weighting scheme, or an explicit no-weighting statement
Classification of criteria as mandatory or compensatory
preconditions: Objectives and constraints have been framed
Each criterion is stated in terms that permit a result to be recorded against it
effects: Alternatives can be scored against a fixed and citable criterion set
Criteria that also act as eligibility filters are linked to the screening criteria
Weighting remains optional so that decisions without a weighting scheme are still complete

functions.name: Evaluate and compare the alternatives
functions.description: Record, as governed decision content, one evaluation round: eligibility screening results with reasons for exclusion, per-criterion results for admitted alternatives, any aggregation and ranking, sensitivity findings, and citations to evidence. Running an executable rule set or decision service to produce those results is outside this model.
inputs: Declared criterion set and screening criteria
Recorded results per alternative and criterion
Evidence item references supporting results or assumptions
outputs: Eligibility and exclusion results with a recorded reason for each exclusion
Alternative-by-criterion comparison matrix for the round
Result status markers for contested, provisional or bias-adjusted results
preconditions: At least one alternative is registered and the criterion set is declared
The evaluation round ordinal is available and has not been used
effects: A serially numbered, append-only evaluation round is recorded and never edited in place
Every excluded alternative carries an explicit recorded reason
Cited evidence is bound by identifier and role only; evidence appraisal, integrity and provenance stay with the evidence model
Execution traces of any external decision service are not captured here
