exceptions: Publicly disclosed registry facts may be served without an individual grant where the source licence permits redistribution and required attribution is attached.
Protected or suppressed values flagged by an authority's protection regime are withheld even from otherwise authorised callers, and the withholding is reported as an omission with a reason.
Emergency or statutory disclosure to a competent authority may bypass the standard grant path but must be recorded with the legal basis, the requesting authority and the scope released.
The organization's own steward may read the full record about that organization, excluding third-party personal data and licensed source content whose terms forbid onward disclosure.
Ownership and beneficial-ownership statements follow the publishing licence attached to their statement set, which may be narrower than the organization record's default class.
Statutory open-register extracts may be disclosed without a private grant when the source register is public.
A successor or acquiring organization may read lineage of a ceased predecessor needed to complete the corporate action.
Non-public contact channels are visible only to organization-steward and agents with a legal-notices exception.
Quality-exception payloads (failed corroboration) are visible to compliance-reader even when full presence detail is not.
audit_requirements: Every read of a restricted, licensed or personal-data-bearing scope is logged with caller identity, scope, projection, policy version and RFC 3339 timestamp.
Every grant issuance, modification and revocation is logged with the authorising agent, purpose, scope and validity period.
Every merge, split, correction, deletion and erasure writes an append-only entry that cannot be edited, only superseded.
Audit entries are retained at least as long as the data they describe, and their own deletion requires separate authorisation recorded outside the deleted scope.
Access logs are themselves classified as personal-data-bearing where they identify natural persons and are minimised accordingly.
Every compliance-profile read records requester, purpose, projection and datetime.
Every create or update of legal name, legal identifier, legal form, status or successor links records actor, evidence reference, effective time and recorded time.
Identifier resolution that returns DUPLICATE, ANNULLED or successor-required must be auditable.

read_order: AGENTS.md first, to obtain Name, Type, Specification URL, Storage type URL, Interface URL and Processes URL before touching any data — this holds even when the storage is MongoDB or the interface is MCP, because the bootstrap contract is storage- and interface-neutral.
Specification URL next, to load the model semantics: scope, boundaries, bundles, layers, findings, data elements and artifact rules.
Storage type URL, to learn how the semantic record is projected into the concrete store, including canonicalization, versioning and digest conventions.
Interface URL, to learn the available operations, projections, scopes and error semantics before attempting any read or write.
Processes URL, to learn the governed procedures for ingestion, resolution, lifecycle assertion, quality assessment, disclosure and retention.
Pinned code list versions and the disclosure and retention policy version, before writing any coded value or publishing any projection.

coverage.claim: The synthesized WM-ORG-001 covers the organization as an externally addressable subject: designation and name history, scheme-qualified identity and canonical key selection, legal form and entity category, formality spectrum and home legal jurisdiction, activity and statistical classification, declared purpose and scale, formation, registry entry, standing and recurring obligations, lifecycle events, succession, dissolution, organization-side control and ownership endpoints, official roles and affiliation, presence and reachability, and record provenance, stewardship, quality, disclosure, retention and interoperability. Coverage is strongest for registered legal entities in jurisdictions carried by the GLEIF registration-authority and ELF lists and for European classification schemes; it is demonstrably weaker for informal, customary, religious and indigenous collectives, for North American activity classification, and for redomiciliation and post-strike-off restoration. No claim of universal or metaphysical completeness is made.

checklist.notes: Scheme-qualified identifiers, canonical key priority (master-system, governed global/IRI, dimension-assigned UUID/ULID), alias retention, name forms and entity resolution with recorded evidence and confidence. Grounded in LEI-CDF, the ISO 6523 ICD register, BODS identifiers and the EU requirement that the EUID be ISO 6523 compliant.

Formation act and creation date, entity status separated from record registration status with real enumerations, qualified status detail, recurring obligations with due dates and lapse consequences, lifecycle event journal and succession/continuity decisions. Grounded in LEI-CDF LegalEntityEvents, Companies House status enumerations and W3C ORG ChangeEvent.

Consolidation, branch and fund links with typed periods, quantifiers and eight exception reasons; ownership and beneficial-ownership interests with direct/indirect, share ranges and component records for indirect chains; official roles and non-controlling affiliations kept separate. Grounded in RR-CDF, BODS and ISO 5009.

RFC 3339 with seconds and explicit offset or Z; event time, authority recording time and observation/ingestion time held separately and never inferred from one another; validity intervals on names, forms, appointments, sites and interests; three distinct relationship period types; as-at historical reads.

Per-assertion source, source type, licence, retrieval timestamp and asserting agent; derivation typed as copy, revision, transformation or inference; a provenance graph artifact using PROV-O starting-point and qualified terms with prov:Organization as agent.

Two senses are distinguished and both covered: ownership of the organization (interests, beneficial ownership, consolidation, global decision centre) and ownership of the record (steward role, asserting agent, publisher, licence).

Graded corroboration (pending, entity-supplied-only, partially corroborated, fully corroborated) against a named validation authority with validation documents; identifier syntax and check-character rules; version-tag concurrency; partial-data markers; explicit non-match records.

Deny-by-default with grants scoped to bundle, layer, finding and artifact; five named exception classes including authority-suppressed values and statutory disclosure; audit requirements on reads, grants and mutations; projections report omitted fields rather than dropping them silently.

Per-disclosure-class retention with evidenced triggers, statutory minimum checks, field-group minimisation for personal data instead of record deletion, tombstones that keep prior references resolvable, and irreversible action evidence records. Hard deletion of organization records is prohibited by default.

Alignment-not-conformance policy, versioned mapping tables with relation types and declared semantic loss, activity-scheme correspondence tables with mapping cardinality, status-value mapping with loss notes, and a conflict register with per-consumer precedence rules.

Legal form (ISO 20275 with reserved 8888/9999), entity category and subcategory, legal personality, activity codes under versioned schemes, statistical unit alignment, size class and non-profit status.

Jurisdiction constrained to ISO 3166-1/-2 via the accepted jurisdictions list, registered versus operating locations, branches, served areas and delegation of geometry to the place model. Address language and script are treated as first-class.

Registration authorities from a governed 232-jurisdiction list, validation authority, official organizational roles tied to legal form with representation powers and joint-signature rules, granting authorities for non-profit status, and statutory or treaty formation for public bodies.

Personal data held by reference only, disclosure classes per field group, minimisation before projection, authority protection and suppression flags, and correction/erasure request handling with evidenced outcomes.

Absence is modelled as data with reasons and review dates: reserved legal-form codes, reporting exception reasons for unreportable parents, unspecified-entity reasons in ownership, unknown-date markers, registration-not-applicable for informal organizations.
Size and relationship quantifiers carry method, unit, reference period and producing party, with consolidation scope declared; match confidence is expressed on a named scale.

Transport security, authentication mechanisms, key management and integrity signing beyond content digests are deliberately not modelled here. They belong to the storage and interface projections and to platform service models; no cited primary source in this set governs them at the semantic layer, so asserting structure would be unsupported.

Eleven governed functions with preconditions and effects cover resolution, ingestion, event assertion, continuity evaluation, deduplication, classification migration, relationship recording, standing evaluation, projection publication, retention action and standard mapping.

known_omissions: Informal, customary, religious and indigenous organizations are structurally accommodated (registration is optional, identity can rest on a dimension-assigned key) but are not positively grounded: none of the cited primary sources model them, so the treatment is a designed accommodation rather than an evidenced structure.

Financial standing, credit, sanctions and watchlist status are omitted. They are consumer-specific assessments over this record, change on a different cadence, and would import licensing and accuracy obligations that do not belong to organizational identity.
Trademark and trade-name rights over organization names are omitted; the naming layer records name forms and validity but makes no claim about who is entitled to use a name.

Internal governance procedure — board composition rules, quorum, voting and delegation mechanics — is referenced to the charter model and not modelled here, so questions about how a decision was validly taken cannot be answered from this model alone.

Digital-identity credentials for organizations (verifiable credentials, organizational wallets, vLEI-style role credentials) are not modelled. They were not verifiable from the primary sources retrieved in this pass and would need their own evidenced layer.

Multi-jurisdiction tax identity (VAT group membership, permanent establishment, tax residence) is only touched through identifier schemes; its substantive rules are jurisdiction-specific and belong to a tax model.
Organization-to-organization contractual relationships (joint ventures beyond W3C ORG's OrganizationalCollaboration, consortia, franchise networks) are only weakly covered by the affiliation finding.
Historical and defunct organizations predating modern registers are accommodated by unknown-date markers but have no evidenced identity strategy in the cited sources.
Cross-border redomiciliation/continuation as a standardized event type.
Restoration after administrative strike-off as a global code.
Name reservation and companies in formation before legal personality.
Series LLCs, protected-cell companies and similar internal liability partitions.
DAOs and smart-contract collectives without a register or LEI-eligible contract capacity.
Indigenous nations and polities as sovereigns rather than organizations.
A single global nonprofit/charity classification.
Sanctions, licensing and fitness-to-operate registers.
GLEIF RR-CDF Level 2 parent, fund-relationship and reporting-exception records.
Officer/director registers as a governance model (ISO 5009 roles discovered but not fetched as a governing source).
NAICS as a first-party Bureau source was not fetched; North American activity is a likely regional omission.
Core Public Organisation Vocabulary is a specialized public-body profile not fully expanded here.
conflicts: Directive (EU) 2017/1132 and Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1042 could not be rendered in full by the retrieval tool; the EUID provisions cited in SRC-016 were surfaced from EUR-Lex indexed text rather than a full-text read, and must be verified against the Official Journal before being relied on normatively. This is the weakest evidential link in the model and the EUID-specific data element should be treated as provisional.

FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 on basic company information and beneficial ownership were unreachable (HTTP 403) in this pass. The beneficial-ownership structure therefore rests on BODS, an authority-tier-2 standard, rather than on the intergovernmental requirement it implements; the ownership layer should be re-grounded when FATF text is retrievable.

Status vocabularies conflict irreconcilably across sources: LEI-CDF uses a two-value entity status plus a ten-value registration status, while Companies House uses a twelve-value national enumeration mixing legal states (dissolved, liquidation) with record states (removed, open). Any normalised status is lossy, which is why the model requires both the source value and the mapping loss note to be retained.

'Organization' scope conflicts between sources: W3C ORG admits informal collectives, LEI-CDF is restricted to entities that can be validated against a registration authority, and BODS distinguishes registeredEntity from legalEntity, arrangement, anonymousEntity and unknownEntity. This model takes the broad W3C reading and treats registry-backed structure as conditional.

Legal form and activity classification are jurisdiction-bound and revision-bound: the same organization can hold non-equivalent NACE and ISIC codes, and a legal form may exist only at ISO 3166-2 subdivision level. Cross-scheme comparison without a declared correspondence table and mapping cardinality is unsound.

Statistical enterprise boundaries follow control while legal-unit boundaries follow legal personality, so official statistics and legal registers will legitimately disagree about how many organizations exist in a group. The model records this as alignment and forbids using statistical units to merge or split records.
W3C ORG recommends one legally recognized skos:prefLabel; RegOrg and CBV allow multiple legalName values in multilingual jurisdictions; LEI-CDF allows one Primary LegalName plus OtherEntityNames.
ORG identifier is a typed literal; RegOrg/CBV require a structured ADMS Identifier; both can be derived in one direction only.
LEI EntityStatus, LEI RegistrationStatus and national orgStatus vocabularies are three different state machines often wrongly merged.
NACE Rev. 2, NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 4 and ISIC Rev. 5 are related but not interchangeable; schema.org still cites ISIC Rev. 4.
ELF codes are unique per jurisdiction-form pair; similarly named forms (SA, LLC, GmbH) are not equivalent across borders.
AssociatedEntity is deprecated in LEI-CDF 3.1 in favour of events and relationship records.
A GLEIF BRANCH category is not an org:OrganizationalUnit and not necessarily an org:Site.
CBV/RegOrg exclude informal organizations that W3C ORG and this catalogue purpose explicitly include.
regional_assumptions: The registration and standing bundle is strongest for jurisdictions covered by the GLEIF registration-authority list (232 jurisdictions, 1,050+ registers); coverage depth, update cadence and data quality vary sharply between them and are not uniform.

Activity classification assumes access to NACE Rev. 2.1 (European statistics from 2025) or ISIC Rev. 5 (endorsed 2023); jurisdictions on older revisions or on wholly national schemes require correspondence tables that may be one-to-many.

The EUID and BRIS interconnection provisions apply only to EU member-state registers and to companies and branches within their scope; they are not a global identifier mechanism and must not be assumed elsewhere.

Electronic addressing examples derive from a European business network; the scheme-designator plus value pattern generalises, but the specific designators and the availability of a participant registry do not.

The personal-data treatment assumes a jurisdiction with data-protection obligations over officer and beneficial-owner data and with a correction/erasure route; jurisdictions with full public disclosure of officer data, or with none, will need different disclosure classes.
Non-profit and public-benefit status is granted per jurisdiction under non-comparable criteria; the status code is only interpretable together with its granting jurisdiction and instrument.
Latin-script assumptions are avoided in the model but persist in several cited code lists, which supply transliterations rather than treating non-Latin forms as primary.
Home legal jurisdiction can be expressed as ISO 3166-1 or 3166-2.
Where a business register exists, it is the master for legal name, legal identifier and national legal form.
EU interoperability prefers NACE; global statistical comparison prefers ISIC; other regions use national schemes mapped to ISIC.
LEI is widely available for contract-capable entities but is not mandatory for all organization types or informal collectives.
ELF list v1.6 still uses reserved 8888/9999 where research is incomplete, including some legal forms not yet enumerated.
French overseas territories sharing French legislation inherit French ELF codes and legal jurisdiction France, per GLEIF ELF notes.
Public access to company extracts varies; UK/EU open-register practice must not be assumed for all states.
adversarial_checks: Counterexample — organization without any register: community groups, unincorporated associations and informal collectives have no registry entry, no legal form code and no scheme identifier. The model survives because registration, legal form and standing are optional, identity may rest on a dimension-assigned UUID/ULID, and the entity-category finding forces the applicability question explicitly. A structure that required a registration number would have been rejected.

Counterexample — branch with its own identifier but no legal personality: a branch can hold an LEI under EntityCategory BRANCH while being legally part of another entity. This breaks any rule equating 'has a global identifier' with 'is a legal person', so legal personality is modelled as a separate flag and the branch link is a typed relationship rather than internal containment.

Counterexample — one organization, many contradictory registers: a multinational may be simultaneously ACTIVE in a global index and 'liquidation' in a national register, with different legal names in each. Rather than picking a winner, the model requires the conflict to be recorded with both sources and resolved per consumer through a precedence rule, and forbids overwriting a more strongly corroborated value during bulk refresh.

Rejected structure — a single 'status' field: attractive and near-universal in practice, but LEI-CDF's separation of entity status from registration status plus Companies House's mixed enumeration prove that at least two independent state machines exist. A single field was rejected as unsupported and actively lossy.

Rejected structure — 'organization = legal unit': Eurostat register practice shows an enterprise may span several legal units and that group boundaries follow control. Equating the organization with the legal unit would have made statistical alignment impossible, so statistical unit type became a classification with an explicit prohibition on using it to merge or split records.

Rejected structure — name-based or address-based identity: names are non-unique within and across registers, change without identity change, and exist in multiple scripts; addresses are shared by thousands of service-provided entities. Both were excluded from every identity strategy, and the artifact rules state this explicitly.

Rejected structure — folding beneficial ownership persons into this model: it would import personal-data retention, minimisation and access obligations onto the organization record. BODS's separation of entity, person and relationship records supports delegating person records, so only organization-side endpoints are kept.

Stress test — silent absence: a naive model represents a missing parent, an unlisted legal form and a suppressed address all as null. The cited sources supply four distinct mechanisms (eight reporting exception reasons, reserved codes 8888/9999, unspecified-entity reasons, authority suppression flags), so explicit absence-with-reason was made a policy rather than a convention.

Stress test — conformance inflation: it would be easy to claim conformance to W3C ORG, ISO 17442 and schema.org simultaneously. No test or certification evidence was retrieved for any of them, so all are recorded as ALIGN or REFERENCE, and the mapping function is required to attach an alignment-not-conformance notice.
Informal community versus registered company: refusing a fake company number while still assigning a Dimension id and names.
Lapsed LEI versus dissolved entity: a non-renewed identifier must not be treated as cessation.
Duplicate LEI exclusivity violation: DUPLICATE status marks the non-surviving identifier, not a second organization.
International branch with own LEI versus a mere site of headquarters.
Merger where the surviving legal entity keeps its id versus a new entity that must receive a new canonical id.
Two official legal names in a bilingual jurisdiction versus a translation stored as a trading name.
Subsidiary that is a full Organization versus a department modelled as WM-ORG-002.
Government ministry that can contract without incorporation, eligible for LEI as RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY.
Sole proprietor where the human person is a sibling and only the business capacity is this subject.
Activity code copied from an old NACE Rev. 2 filing after the statistical program moved to Rev. 2.1 without correspondence.

boundaryDecision.rationale: Both providers independently returned entry_kind 'entity' and the subject behaves as one: a persistent, externally addressable subject bearing identity, classification, standing and a lifecycle, not an event, relation or service. The one live boundary divergence is control and ownership: the base retains organization-side endpoints of consolidation, group and beneficial-ownership relationship records while Grok delegates them entirely to a sibling. Adjudicated in favour of the base, because BODS itself separates entity records, person records and relationship records, so keeping only the entity-side endpoint is evidenced rather than invented, and the base already delegates person records with their distinct privacy, access and retention obligations. The ownership layer is nonetheless marked as the seam to re-test when the sibling relationship model is registered, so this acceptance is of the base's endpoint-only reading, not of a full relationship model living inside WM-ORG-001.

decisions.concept: Base provider selection
decisions.rationale: Nine evidenced neighbor notes, each carrying an operational discrimination test for the hard cases (branch holding its own LEI, statistical enterprise spanning legal units, sole proprietor, register-as-institution, fund and sub-fund, informal collectives, BODS person records, site and place), plus explicit prohibition rules. Grok's boundary is cleaner only where it delegates ownership wholesale, and it leaves umbrella, branch and successor relations half-inside. Size was not the deciding factor.

decisions.concept: Control and ownership inside the organization model
decisions.disposition: Base reading retained; endpoint-only scope confirmed
decisions.rationale: Grok places beneficial ownership, shareholding and GLEIF Level 2 records entirely out of scope. The base keeps only the organization-side endpoints, which BODS supports by separating entity, person and relationship records. Retaining the endpoint preserves group and consolidation answerability without importing person-level privacy, access and retention obligations.

decisions.concept: Home legal jurisdiction as a first-class finding
decisions.rationale: The base makes legal form jurisdiction-dependent and cites the accepted-jurisdictions code list, yet never establishes the jurisdiction of formation as its own fact, leaving a dangling dependency and no answer for multi-register countries.

decisions.concept: Organization formality spectrum
decisions.rationale: The base declares a broad W3C ORG reading that admits informal collectives but implements it only as an exception question under a GLEIF category vocabulary. The W3C ORG, RegOrg and CBV three-step spectrum gives that reading real structure.

decisions.concept: National legal form vocabulary alongside ELF
decisions.rationale: ELF is a cross-border alignment and does not replace the home register's own form code when that register is master; the cross-border false-equivalence guard for SA, LLC and GmbH is absent from the base.

decisions.concept: Dissolution as a terminal state distinct from succession
decisions.rationale: The base models termination only as a transition to a successor and cannot represent cessation without one, winding-up in progress, or the rule that identifiers remain historical keys and are never reassigned.

decisions.concept: Record stewardship and change authority
decisions.rationale: The base's checklist claims steward coverage that no finding implements; per-field-group master assignment and authorised change agents are distinct from provenance attribution.

decisions.concept: LEI and global identifier scheme specifics (grok lei-and-global-schemes)
decisions.rationale: The ISO 17442 eligibility test and LEI exclusivity rule are genuinely unanswerable from the base's generic scheme-qualified identifier finding, but Grok's evidence is an ISO catalogue landing page, not the normative text, and a scheme-specific finding would cut against the base's deliberate format-neutral generalisation. Re-open once ISO 17442-1:2020 normative text is readable.

decisions.concept: National standing codes (grok national-standing-codes)
decisions.rationale: The base's entity-status-vs-registration-status finding already asks for qualifying status detail and the governing procedure for administration, liquidation and struck-off-pending, and already requires the source value plus a mapping loss note. Only the restoration and redomiciliation gap is genuinely new, and both providers agree no primary cross-jurisdictional schema exists for it, so it moves to deferred research rather than into structure.

decisions.concept: Primary versus secondary activity (grok primary-versus-secondary-activity)
decisions.rationale: The base's activity-code-assignments finding already asks which activity is principal and by what criterion principality was determined, and separately asks whether the code was assigned by the organization, a register or a statistical authority.

decisions.concept: Contact channels (grok contact-channels)
decisions.rationale: The base's electronic-addresses-and-channels finding already covers channel purpose including legal service, per-channel verification, and retirement with redirect or tombstone, on a stronger scheme-qualified footing than the schema.org-backed alternative.

decisions.concept: Non-activity classifications (grok non-activity-classifications)
decisions.disposition: Rejected as weakly supported and overlapping
decisions.rationale: Charity and nonprofit status is already carried by the base's purpose-and-nonprofit-status finding with a granting authority and instrument. The remaining taxonomic-scheme content rests on W3C ORG plus a tier-3 schema.org reference, and Grok itself records the absence of any cross-border nonprofit classification as a gap.

decisions.concept: Multiple co-equal legal names in multilingual jurisdictions
decisions.disposition: Accepted as a required correction to the base naming finding, not as a new finding
decisions.rationale: RegOrg and SEMIC CBV make legalName a repeatable language-tagged literal precisely because bilingual jurisdictions grant several legal names of equal standing, which contradicts the base question asking which single name form is the legal name. Adding Grok's finding would duplicate name-forms-and-validity, so this is recorded as a framing correction and carried as a publication hold instead.

decisions.concept: Alternative-name integrity rule
decisions.disposition: Accepted as a constraint on the base naming layer, not as a new finding
decisions.rationale: RegOrg and CBV forbid storing a translation of the legal name in an alternative or trading name field. The base already separates name kinds and language tags but states no such prohibition, and a prohibition is a rule on an existing finding rather than a finding of its own.

decisions.concept: Grok functions
decisions.rationale: resolve-identifier, record-legal-entity-event and validate-current-standing map one-to-one onto the base's resolve-organization-identifier, assert-lifecycle-event and evaluate-record-standing; syndicate-directory-card and disclose-registry-extract are scoped emissions already covered by publish-projection; construct-succession-lineage is the read side of evaluate-succession-continuity and the lineage view publish-projection already names. No function addition would add capability.

decisions.concept: Statistical unit alignment
decisions.disposition: Retained from base; no Grok equivalent
decisions.rationale: Grok has no counterpart to the Eurostat business-register distinction between legal unit, enterprise and enterprise group, nor to the prohibition on using statistical units to merge or split organization records. This is a base-only strength that the synthesis must preserve intact.

decisions.concept: schema.org source classification disagreement
decisions.rationale: The base records schema.org as a primary source at authority tier 2 while Grok records it as non-primary at tier 3. Grok's classification is the defensible one for a community vocabulary used as a discovery mapping, and both models already treat it as alignment rather than conformance.

decisions.concept: Security dimension
decisions.rationale: The base marks transport security, authentication, key management and integrity signing as deliberately unmodelled because no cited primary source governs them at the semantic layer. Grok asserts no structure there either, so the honest declared gap is carried forward rather than papered over.

publicationHolds: Source and live-version verification is incomplete and must be run before publication: every accepted source URL must be re-fetched and its version pin confirmed. The two providers cite different GLEIF URL paths for the same two documents (LEI-CDF 3.1 under /common-data-file-format/current-versions/ versus /common-data-file-format/, and the ELF list under /code-lists/ versus the bare path), so at least one variant in each pair is stale or a redirect and the canonical form must be established.

Multi-profile domain validation has not been performed. The structure must be exercised against at least six distinct profiles before publication: a registered company with an LEI, an unregistered informal collective with no scheme identifier, an international branch holding its own LEI without separate legal personality, a fund with an umbrella and management relationship, a resident government entity formed by statute, and a sole proprietor whose legal person is a natural person. Coverage claims are provisional until each profile is walked end to end.

The EUID and BRIS provisions carried by Commission Implementing Regulation (EU) 2021/1042 were surfaced from indexed EUR-Lex text rather than a full-text read, by the base provider's own admission. The EUID-specific data element must be treated as provisional and verified against the Official Journal before any normative reliance.

FATF Recommendations 24 and 25 were unreachable (HTTP 403), so the beneficial-ownership structure rests on BODS at authority tier 2 rather than on the intergovernmental requirement it implements. The ownership layer must be re-grounded before it is published as an authority-backed structure.

The base naming finding asks which single name form is the legal name, which is wrong for multilingual jurisdictions where RegOrg and SEMIC CBV make legalName a repeatable language-tagged literal with several co-equal legal names. The naming layer must be reframed to admit multiple co-equal legal names, with the RegOrg prohibition on storing translations in alternative-name fields, before that layer is published as normative.

ISO 17442-1:2020 and ISO 20275 were cited from standards-catalogue landing pages, not normative text. Any statement in the synthesized model that reads as a conformance or eligibility rule derived from those standards must be marked alignment-only until the normative text is obtained.

ISO 5009 is carried by the base as a tier-1 primary source for official organizational roles while the other provider records it as discovered but not fetched. The official-roles finding's specific claims (role counts, jurisdiction coverage, tie to ELF, exclusion of internal functional titles) must be confirmed against the fetched code list before publication.
deferredResearch: ISO 17442-1:2020 normative text, to ground LEI eligibility (whether the subject can enter contracts or is legally or financially responsible) and LEI exclusivity and non-reassignment as evidenced constraints. If confirmed, re-open the deferred grok finding lei-and-global-schemes for placement in the identifier-schemes-and-keys layer.

Cross-border redomiciliation and continuation, and restoration after administrative strike-off, as event types. Both providers independently record that no primary cross-jurisdictional schema exists, so these currently sit as event hooks with no code list; find whether any regional instrument (EU mobility directive, US continuance statutes) supplies a citable vocabulary.

NAICS from a first-party Bureau source, and the NAICS-to-ISIC correspondence. North American activity classification is a known regional omission and the activity layer is currently European-weighted through NACE.

Core Public Organisation Vocabulary as the specialised public-body profile, to test whether the government and international-organization subjects currently handled through the GLEIF entity category and subcategory need their own evidenced structure.

Organizational digital-identity credentials (verifiable credentials, organizational wallets, vLEI role credentials). Not verifiable from either retrieval pass and would need its own evidenced layer rather than being folded into identifier schemes.

Series LLCs, protected-cell companies and comparable internal liability partitions, and DAOs or smart-contract collectives without a register or contract capacity. These stress the formality spectrum and the legal-personality flag and are currently recorded as gaps by both providers.

Whether the ownership and control layer should remain in WM-ORG-001 as organization-side endpoints or move to a dedicated relationship sibling once that model is registered. Re-test the seam at sibling registration time rather than pre-emptively splitting now.

bundles.name: Identity and designation
bundles.description: Everything needed to say which organization is being referred to: its names across time, language and script; its identifiers under external schemes; the canonical key the adopting Dimension uses; and the evidence needed to resolve or reject a candidate match.
bundles.rationale: W3C ORG models identifier and naming as first-class but under-specified properties; LEI-CDF, the ISO 6523 ICD register and BODS all show that a usable organization identity is a scheme-qualified pair plus temporal name history, not a single string. Duplicate resolution is a distinct concern because LEI registration explicitly carries a DUPLICATE status, proving that identity collisions occur in governed registries.

layers.name: Naming and designations
layers.description: Legal, trading, former, abbreviated and transliterated names of the organization, each with language, script, kind and validity in time.

findings.name: Name forms, kinds and validity periods
findings.description: An organization carries several simultaneous name forms with different legal weight. LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalName from OtherEntityNames, schema.org separates legalName from name and alternateName, and BODS separates name from alternateNames. Each form needs a kind, a language tag, and an explicit validity interval because names change without changing identity.

findings.name: Name history and change tracking
findings.description: Former names must remain retrievable and ordered, because lookups, sanctions screening and lineage tracing rely on historical strings. Companies House exposes previous_company_names as a first-class array and LEI-CDF carries name changes inside LegalEntityEvents; a purely current-state name model loses answerable history.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Name history is derived from lifecycle event records and name evidence records already held elsewhere in this model; it is an ordered projection over those artifacts, so materialising a separate artifact would duplicate evidence and create a second place for the same facts to drift.

layers.name: Identifier schemes and canonical keys
layers.description: Externally issued, scheme-qualified identifiers for the organization, and the internal canonical key used when no authoritative identifier exists.

findings.name: Scheme-qualified external identifiers
findings.description: An organization identifier is meaningless without its scheme. ISO 6523 ICD codes pair a numeric scheme designator with a value (0199 for LEI, 0060 for D-U-N-S, 0208 for the Belgian enterprise number); LEI-CDF pairs RegistrationAuthorityID with RegistrationAuthorityEntityID; BODS requires id plus scheme/schemeName or uri; and the EU EUID must itself be ISO 6523 compliant.

findings.name: Canonical key selection and internal identity
findings.description: Because many organizations hold several external identifiers and many hold none, the model must state a deterministic priority for choosing the canonical key: authoritative master-system identifier first, then a governed global identifier or IRI, then a UUID or ULID assigned by the adopting Dimension. Dates, names and addresses are never keys.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The canonical key and its priority tier are pure record metadata carried inline on the organization record; there is no external document to retain, and materialising a key artifact would create an independently mutable copy of the very value that must be immutable.

findings.name: Entity resolution, matching evidence and duplicates
findings.description: Governed registries themselves record duplicates — LEI RegistrationStatus includes DUPLICATE, and Companies House exposes partial_data_available and etag for concurrency. A defensible model therefore records the evidence, method and confidence behind every merge or split rather than asserting a silent match.

bundles.name: Classification, legal form and declared purpose
bundles.description: How the organization is typed by governed code lists (legal form, entity category, activity, statistical unit) and what it declares about its own purpose, non-profit character and scale.
bundles.rationale: Legal form (ISO 20275), activity (NACE Rev. 2.1, ISIC Rev. 5) and entity category (LEI-CDF) are all governed, versioned, jurisdiction-bound code lists whose assignments carry their own validity and evidence. Eurostat's register manual shows that statistical unit type is a separate classification that must not be confused with identity. Purpose and scale are self-declared and therefore need a different evidence treatment from coded classifications.

layers.name: Legal form and entity category
layers.description: The organization's legal form under its jurisdiction of formation, its entity category and subcategory, and whether it has separate legal personality at all.

findings.name: Entity legal form assignment
findings.description: Legal form is a four-character ELF code valid only in combination with a jurisdiction, drawn from a list of more than 3,600 forms across more than 200 jurisdictions. The reserved codes 8888 (form not yet listed) and 9999 (no separate legal form) make the absence of a form explicitly representable rather than null.
findings.inline_only_rationale: The legal form assignment is a coded reference into an externally governed list; the authoritative artifact is the ELF code list itself, which is maintained upstream and referenced by version rather than copied, and the evidencing constitutive document is already held by the formation-act finding.

findings.name: Entity category, subcategory and legal personality
findings.description: LEI-CDF categorises entities as BRANCH, GENERAL, FUND, SOLE_PROPRIETOR, RESIDENT_GOVERNMENT_ENTITY or INTERNATIONAL_ORGANIZATION, with government subcategories. Category determines which other findings are even applicable and whether the subject has separate legal personality — a branch and a sole proprietorship do not.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Category and personality are coded assertions evaluated against the constitutive act and register record; both evidencing artifacts already exist in the formation and registry-entry findings, and duplicating them here would split the evidence chain.

findings.name: Organization formality spectrum
findings.description: org:Organization is a collection of people with a common purpose that can act as an agent, including informal communities. org:FormalOrganization is recognized in the world at large, especially in legal jurisdictions, with rights and responsibilities (corporation, charity, government, church). rov:RegisteredOrganization / CBV Legal Entity is a formal organization that gained legal status through a registration process and excludes natural persons, virtual organizations and agents that can act without that registration. Many organizations are not legal entities; some umbrellas contain several legal entities. Unregistered collectives remain in scope of this model as Organization, not as RegisteredOrganization.

findings.name: National legal form vocabulary
findings.description: Each jurisdiction maintains a limited set of recognized company or entity types (Plc, GmbH, SA, LLP and so on). Lexically identical labels can have different legal meanings across borders. RegOrg orgType and CBV legal form type are SKOS/code list specializations of org:classification. ELF is the cross-border alignment, not a replacement for the national register's form code when that register is the master system.

layers.name: Activity and statistical classification
layers.description: Coded economic-activity assignments under versioned schemes, and the organization's relationship to statistical units used by official registers.

findings.name: Activity code assignments across schemes
findings.description: Activity classification is scheme-bound and revision-bound: NACE Rev. 2.1 applies to European statistics from 2025 under Regulation (EC) No 1893/2006 and Delegated Regulation (EU) 2023/137, ISIC Rev. 5 was endorsed in 2023, and national registers use their own lists such as UK SIC. An assignment without its scheme version is not interpretable.

findings.name: Statistical unit alignment
findings.description: Official registers hold enterprise group, enterprise and local unit as mandatory statistical units alongside legal units and their links, because an enterprise may span several legal units and group boundaries follow control rather than legal personality. Recording this alignment prevents an agent from silently merging legal units into one organization or splitting an organization to match a statistical unit.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Statistical unit alignment is an assertion linking this record to units held in an external statistical register; the authoritative artifact is that register's own record, which is not redistributable in most jurisdictions, so only the reference and its provenance are retained.

layers.name: Declared purpose and scale
layers.description: What the organization states about its own mission, non-profit character and size, and how those self-declarations are dated and evidenced.

findings.name: Declared purpose, object clause and non-profit status
findings.description: W3C ORG models purpose as a first-class property and schema.org exposes nonprofitStatus and ownershipFundingInfo. Purpose statements are either constitutive (an object clause in the charter) or self-declared marketing text, and the two carry very different weight; non-profit status is a jurisdiction-granted determination, not a self-description.

findings.name: Scale, workforce and size-class measures
findings.description: Size indicators such as headcount are measurements with a method, unit, reference period and source, not static attributes. schema.org exposes numberOfEmployees and statistical registers hold size variables; without a reference period and a counting basis (headcount, full-time equivalent, including or excluding contractors) the figure is not comparable.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Size measures are reported values whose evidencing documents (annual accounts, statistical returns) belong to reporting and financial models outside this scope; retaining a separate artifact here would duplicate filings already covered by the recurring-obligations finding.

bundles.name: Formation, registration standing and lifecycle
bundles.description: How the organization came into existence, where it is recorded, what its current standing is, what recurring obligations keep that standing alive, and how it changes or ends.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF separates EntityStatus from RegistrationStatus, proving that the subject's existence and the record's standing are independent state machines; Companies House adds a twelve-value national status enumeration plus status detail; W3C ORG models ChangeEvent with originalOrganization and resultedFrom for succession; and the EU BRIS regime requires a register-issued identifier for companies and branches. These are distinct, separately answerable concerns.

layers.name: Formation and registry entries
layers.description: The constitutive act that created the organization and the entries that public and private registers hold about it.

findings.name: Formation act and creation date
findings.description: LEI-CDF records EntityCreationDate as the legal establishment date, schema.org records foundingDate and foundingLocation, BODS records foundingDate and formedByStatute, and Companies House records date_of_creation. Formation date and first registration date are frequently different and must not be conflated.

findings.name: Registry entry and registration authority
findings.description: An entry links the organization to an authoritative source through a register code plus a local entity number, as in LEI-CDF's RegistrationAuthorityID and RegistrationAuthorityEntityID, drawing on a governed list of more than 1,050 registers across 232 jurisdictions. The EU adds the EUID, which must be ISO 6523 compliant and unequivocally identify companies and branches across interconnected registers.

findings.name: Home legal jurisdiction
findings.description: LEI-CDF LegalJurisdiction is the jurisdiction of legal formation and registration and is the jurisdiction on which LegalForm depends. It is an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 country code or an ISO 3166-2 region code, uppercase. French overseas territories sharing French legal forms are treated as France for legal jurisdiction in the ELF list implementation. Home jurisdiction is not necessarily the headquarters country or the tax residence.

layers.name: Standing, status and recurring obligations
layers.description: The organization's current legal standing, the separate standing of each record about it, and the periodic acts required to keep both current.

findings.name: Entity status distinguished from record registration status
findings.description: LEI-CDF keeps EntityStatus (ACTIVE, INACTIVE, NULL — whether the entity is legally registered and operating) strictly separate from RegistrationStatus (PENDING_VALIDATION, ISSUED, DUPLICATE, LAPSED, RETIRED, ANNULLED, CANCELLED, TRANSFERRED, PENDING_TRANSFER, PENDING_ARCHIVAL — the standing of the record). Companies House adds a twelve-value national enumeration plus company_status_detail. Collapsing these into one status field destroys answerability.

findings.name: Recurring filing and renewal obligations
findings.description: Standing is maintained by periodic acts: LEI records carry NextRenewalDate and lapse if not renewed, and national registers require confirmation statements and accounts with their own due dates. Missing a due date changes record standing without changing the organization's existence.

layers.name: Lifecycle events and succession
layers.description: Discrete events that change the organization or its record, and the lineage links that connect predecessor and successor organizations.

findings.name: Lifecycle event records
findings.description: LEI-CDF v3.1 introduced LegalEntityEvents as a container carrying event type, dates, validation documents and the fields affected. W3C ORG models ChangeEvent linked by changedBy and resultedFrom. An event record must separate the date the event legally took effect from the date it was recorded and the date it was observed.

findings.name: Succession, continuity and lineage
findings.description: W3C ORG treats an organization resulting from a change event as sufficiently distinct to have its own identity, linked to originalOrganization; LEI-CDF carries SuccessorEntity with SuccessorLEI or SuccessorEntityName; Eurostat register practice defines continuity rules for unit births and deaths. The hard question is when a change preserves identity and when it creates a new subject.

findings.name: Dissolution and expiry
findings.description: An organization ceases as a subject by dissolution, completion of winding-up, or replacement through corporate action. schema.org dissolutionDate is a secondary discovery field. LEI RETIRED means the entity ceased without merger; INACTIVE covers closure, acquisition or illegitimacy. Identifier records are not reused. History remains queryable after cessation. Deletion of the subject record is a retention decision, not an automatic consequence of dissolution.

bundles.name: Control, ownership and representation
bundles.description: External relationships that determine who controls the organization, who owns or benefits from it, and who may act for it.
bundles.rationale: RR-CDF defines a normative, period-bounded and quantified model of consolidation and fund relationships with explicit reporting exceptions; BODS defines a statement-based model of ownership and control interests with direct/indirect and share ranges; ISO 5009 supplies codes for official roles tied to legal forms and explicitly excludes internal functional titles. Together they establish that control, ownership and representation are three distinct relationship families with different evidence regimes.

layers.name: Group structure and ownership
layers.description: Consolidation and group membership links, and ownership or control interests including beneficial ownership.

findings.name: Consolidation, branch and fund relationship links
findings.description: RR-CDF records IS_DIRECTLY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_ULTIMATELY_CONSOLIDATED_BY, IS_INTERNATIONAL_BRANCH_OF, IS_FUND-MANAGED_BY, IS_SUBFUND_OF and IS_FEEDER_TO, each with up to three distinct period types, a status, quantifiers with a measurement method, and eight exception reasons for when a parent cannot be reported.

findings.name: Ownership and beneficial-ownership interests
findings.description: BODS models ownership and control as relationship records with a subject entity, an interested party, and an array of interests each carrying type, directOrIndirect, a beneficialOwnershipOrControl flag valid only for natural persons, share values expressible as exact figures or as minimum/maximum ranges, and start and end dates. Indirect chains are represented through component records rather than collapsed edges.

layers.name: Official roles, representation and affiliation
layers.description: Who is empowered to act for the organization under law, and which external bodies the organization is affiliated with or accredited by.

findings.name: Official organizational roles and authorised representation
findings.description: ISO 5009 codes cover over 2,000 official roles across almost 250 legal forms in 89 jurisdictions, are tied to the relevant ELF code, include only roles appearing in local legislation, and explicitly exclude internal functional titles such as Chief Risk Officer. W3C ORG separates Role, Post and Membership. This finding covers the organization-side view: which posts exist and what they authorise, not the persons filling them.

findings.name: External affiliation, membership and accreditation
findings.description: Organizations belong to federations, chambers, standards bodies and networks, and hold accreditations or certifications granted by external bodies. W3C ORG models Membership as an n-ary relation between agent, organization and role; schema.org exposes memberOf and hasCredential. These links are neither ownership nor control and must not be conflated with them.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Affiliation and accreditation evidence is issued and published by the conferring body, which is a separate organization subject; this model retains only the scheme-qualified link, validity and verification endpoint, because copying certificates would create an unmaintained duplicate of another party's authoritative record.

bundles.name: Presence and reachability
bundles.description: Where the organization is legally seated, where it actually operates, and through which electronic addresses and channels it can be reached.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF distinguishes LegalAddress from HeadquartersAddress and OtherAddresses with transliterated variants; W3C ORG separates hasRegisteredSite from hasSite; Companies House exposes registered_office_is_in_dispute and undeliverable_registered_office_address, proving that a registered address is a legal construct that can be contested or non-functional; and Peppol shows that electronic addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity.

layers.name: Locations, sites and channels
layers.description: Registered and operating locations of the organization together with its electronic addresses and public channels, each with a role, validity and reachability status.

findings.name: Registered office and legal address
findings.description: The registered office is the address at which the organization is legally addressable in its jurisdiction of formation; it is frequently not an operating location and may be a service-provider address. National registers record when it is in dispute or undeliverable, which are distinct states from being absent.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Registered address values are carried inline on the organization record and evidenced by the registry extract artifact already retained by the registry-entry finding; geometry, building identity and postal normalisation belong to the referenced place model rather than to a duplicated artifact here.

findings.name: Operating sites, branches and service areas
findings.description: W3C ORG models Site as a place where an organization operates and separates hasSite from hasRegisteredSite. Operating presence is distinct from legal seat: a branch may be separately registered and separately identified, while a site may be purely operational with no registry footprint at all.

findings.name: Electronic addresses and public channels
findings.description: Electronic business addressing uses the same scheme-qualified pattern as identity: a Peppol participant is addressed as an ISO 6523 scheme designator plus a value, for example 0199 with an LEI or 0208 with a Belgian enterprise number. Public channels such as websites and published contact points are separate, weaker assertions that require their own verification.
findings.inline_only_rationale: Electronic addresses are scheme-qualified inline values whose authoritative artifact is the network's own participant registry, queried by resolution rather than copied; retaining a local artifact would produce stale routing data with no way to detect divergence.

bundles.name: Record governance and interoperability
bundles.description: Governance of the organization record itself: where each assertion came from, how well corroborated it is, who may see it, how long it is kept, and how it maps onto external standards.
bundles.rationale: LEI-CDF records ValidationSources with graded corroboration levels and a ValidationAuthority, PROV-O supplies the normative vocabulary for attributing assertions to agents and deriving records from sources, BODS requires per-statement source and publication metadata including licence, and national registers expose concurrency and completeness markers. Standard alignment must be recorded as mapping with declared loss, not as conformance.

layers.name: Provenance, quality, access and retention
layers.description: Per-assertion provenance and corroboration, data-quality assessment, disclosure classification and retention rules for the organization record.

findings.name: Assertion provenance and attribution
findings.description: Every field value is an assertion by some agent from some source at some time. PROV-O supplies wasAttributedTo, wasDerivedFrom, wasGeneratedBy and actedOnBehalfOf with prov:Organization as an agent type; BODS requires source type, url, retrievedAt and assertedBy on each statement. Event time and observation time must be recorded separately.

findings.name: Validation, corroboration level and data quality
findings.description: LEI-CDF grades a record's corroboration as PENDING, ENTITY_SUPPLIED_ONLY, PARTIALLY_CORROBORATED or FULLY_CORROBORATED against a named ValidationAuthority, and RR-CDF carries validation sources, documents and references. Companies House marks partial_data_available and exposes an entity tag for concurrency. Quality is therefore a declared, evidenced grade rather than an assumed property.

findings.name: Disclosure classification, access and retention
findings.description: Organization records mix data that registers publish freely, data that is licensed, and data that identifies natural persons and therefore carries privacy obligations. BODS requires an explicit licence on publication; national registers operate protected-address and secure-officer regimes; and retention must be decided per class rather than for the record as a whole.

findings.name: Record stewards
findings.description: The organization itself, acting through officers, is the steward of its own subject record. Registers hold registrar-stewarded copies. GLEIF ManagingLOU administers the LEI record. CBV legal representatives (via schema.org and related discovery) are not the same as employment posts. This layer records stewardship of data, not corporate governance of people.

layers.name: Interoperability and mapping
layers.description: Declared alignments to external standards and the recorded divergences between sources that assert different values for the same organization.

findings.name: Standard alignment, crosswalks and register divergence
findings.description: External standards are alignments, not conformance claims. W3C ORG, schema.org, LEI-CDF, NACE and ISIC each cover overlapping but non-identical ground, and national registers legitimately disagree with global ones about name, status and address. Divergence must be recorded as an observation with sources, not silently resolved.

model.name: Identity Register
model.purpose: Provide a governed, durable and source-qualified registry pattern for anchoring and resolving identifiers of persons, organizations, devices, services and things without importing their descriptive master data.
model.scope_statement: Owns register and namespace identity, entry anchors, identifier and alias bindings, registration and assignment evidence, assurance, lifecycle, entity-resolution assertions, merge and split lineage, purpose-bound resolution, federation mappings, subject rights, access and retention. Subject profiles, credentials, accounts, authentication factors, keys, authorization decisions, source documents and business lifecycle remain external.
in_scope: Register authority and profile, namespace, identifier scheme, syntax, canonicalization, comparison, uniqueness, persistence, non-reuse and resolver contract
Entry identity and external subject reference, identifier bindings, minimal aliases, assignment and proofing evidence, assurance, quality, conflicts, lifecycle and entity resolution
Federation and loss-aware mappings, purpose-bound projections, privacy, subject rights, access, retention, disposition and safe agent operations
out_of_scope: Person, organization, device, service, thing, credential, account, authentication factor, key, authorization policy, source document or audit-log master lifecycle
Biometric algorithms, credential issuance, authentication execution, access decisions, universal name authority or copying full subject profiles into the register
Guarantees of universal identity truth, cross-register equivalence, legal identity, eligibility or rights that are not established by a named authority and jurisdiction

boundary_notes.neighbor: Person, Organization, Device, Service or Thing
boundary_notes.distinction: The register stores a minimal external subject reference and identity assertions; each subject model owns descriptive, physical, functional and contextual properties.
A credential owns issuer claims and validity; the register may cite it as evidence without becoming its issuer, holder or status list.
An entry or identifier can be linked to an account, authenticator or controlled identifier, but lookup does not prove possession or authorize access.
This pattern records identity-specific candidate matches, equivalence and lineage; descriptive golden-record consolidation remains in domain master-data models.
Resolution and assurance are evidence for external decisions, while the model keeps identity-specific provenance and delegates generic logging and authorization.

functions.name: Establish register and namespace
functions.description: Create the governed register profile, authority, subject scope, identifier scheme and resolution rules.
preconditions: mandate, namespace, scheme syntax, uniqueness and steward validate
effects: a versioned identifier space becomes available without creating subject entries

functions.name: Register subject anchor
functions.description: Create a minimal entry that references an external subject master under evidenced registrar authority.
preconditions: subject kind, registrar, evidence, duplicate check, privacy and expected head validate
effects: one durable anchor is created and registration provenance is appended

functions.name: Assign or bind identifier
functions.description: Mint or bind a scheme-governed identifier to an existing entry with explicit validity and source.
preconditions: syntax, canonical form, uniqueness, non-reuse, authority and evidence validate
effects: a source-qualified identifier binding becomes resolvable

functions.name: Resolve identifier purpose-bound
functions.description: Resolve an identifier to the minimum permitted current projection while preserving ambiguity and source state.
preconditions: scheme, access, status, redirect, ambiguity, freshness and rate policy validate
effects: an attributable result is returned without asserting authentication or authorization

functions.name: Attach evidence and assess assurance
functions.description: Append proofing, assignment or verification evidence and a scope-qualified assurance assessment.
preconditions: source authority, integrity, custody, method version, scope, time and disclosure validate
effects: reliance basis and residual uncertainty become explicit

functions.name: Record match or equivalence assertion
functions.description: Record candidate similarity, same-subject, related or not-same decisions without changing entry identity.
preconditions: privacy, method version, score scale, threshold, evidence, review and relation type validate
effects: identity-resolution evidence is visible and contestable

functions.name: Merge, split, correct or supersede
functions.description: Apply an authorized, evidenced lineage change while preserving prior entries, identifiers and redirects.
outputs: successor revisions, lineage event and tombstones
preconditions: expected heads, evidence, contest status, survivor or children, non-reuse and rollback validate
effects: current resolution changes without erasing identity history

functions.name: Suspend, revoke, retire or reactivate
functions.description: Append a status transition to an entry or binding with reason, authority and effective time.
preconditions: transition guard, authority, reason, effective time, notifications and reversibility validate
effects: current standing changes while prior state and evidence remain

functions.name: Federate, map and project
functions.description: Create a scoped cross-register mapping or standards projection with explicit trust and loss accounting.
preconditions: versions, relation semantics, authority, confidence, disclosure, omissions and round trip validate
effects: another system receives a traceable, loss-aware representation

functions.name: Exercise rights, retain, dispose and audit
functions.description: Process correction or redress and authorized retention or disposition without destroying required lineage.
outputs: rights decision, disposition event or audit evidence
preconditions: requester verification, authority, deadline, legal hold, minimum tombstone and post-write checks validate
effects: rights and records duties are fulfilled with attributable evidence

composition.target: Person, Organization, Device, Service and Thing models
composition.purpose: Resolve the subject without copying its profile or lifecycle.

composition.target: Credential, Account, Authentication, Key, Policy and Source Document models
composition.purpose: Use external proof, control and decision evidence while preserving responsibility boundaries.
Align identity vocabulary, proofing, assurance, federation, risk, privacy and redress concepts.

composition.target: DID Core, Controlled Identifiers and Verifiable Credentials
composition.purpose: Project controlled identifiers, controller and resolution data and credential evidence without universalizing their trust model.

composition.target: GS1 Digital Link and GLEIF LEI formats
composition.purpose: Support product, asset, location and legal-entity identifier profiles with explicit scope and loss accounting.
Represent provenance, identifiers, local UUIDs and explicit event times.

owner_package_requirements: Dimension identity, owner, registrar, namespace authority and accountable privacy and records stewards
Identity-register, subject-kind, identifier-scheme, evidence-method, assurance, federation, rights and retention registries
Master-system mappings for persons, organizations, devices, things, services, credentials, accounts, keys, source documents, policies and audit logs
Registration, uniqueness, non-reuse, entity-resolution, lifecycle, disclosure, federation, redress, retention and agent-operation policies
dimension.namespace_guidance: Mint a Dimension identifier for each register and register-qualified entry. Retain authoritative external subject and scheme identifiers. Never use a name, identifier value, timestamp or digest alone as universal subject identity.
registry_links: https://ver.cy/models/
https://ver.cy/model-agent-protocol.md
Dimension-local register, namespace, scheme, assurance, evidence-method, federation and rights registries

canonicalization_rules: Canonicalize an entry by register identifier plus entry identifier; canonicalize identifier bindings under their named scheme and version, not by display label or ad hoc string normalization.
Canonical representation, comparison, uniqueness scope, persistence and reassignment rules are versioned and cited by every binding.
patch_rules: Extensions declare subject domain, authority, identifier scheme, target finding, required evidence, lifecycle, privacy, interoperability and migration impact.

Changes to namespace meaning, comparison, uniqueness, non-reuse, authoritative scope, equivalence, merge or resolution behavior require a successor profile, migration map and preserved old resolver semantics.
compatibility_rules: Unknown additive fields may be ignored only when entry identity, subject reference, identifier binding, authority, status, time, provenance, access and lineage remain intact.
Every ISO, NIST, DID, CID, VC, GS1 or LEI mapping pins source and target versions and states omissions, collisions, semantic conflicts and round-trip limits.

identity_priority: Authoritative master-system register and entry identifiers qualified by namespace and operator.
Governed globally resolvable URI or sector identifier under a named scheme authority.
Dimension UUID under RFC 9562 when no external or governed global identifier exists.
artifact_rules.timestamp_rule: Use RFC 3339 timestamps with seconds and explicit offset or Z; separate request, registration, assignment, effective, observation, ingestion, correction, resolution and knowledge times.
artifact_rules.serial_naming_rule: Use {register-id}--{scope-id}--{artifact-kind}--{assertion-or-event-id}, where scope-id is register for register-scoped records or the entry identifier for entry-scoped records; never use subject name, identifier value, date or digest alone.
artifact_rules.integrity_rule: Store digest, media type, register and optional entry binding, assertion or event identity, scheme and profile versions, event and knowledge times, authority, access marking and provenance.

policies: An identity register anchors identifiers and source-qualified identity assertions; it does not own the subject profile, credential, account, authentication factor, key, authorization decision or business lifecycle.
Identifier equality, name similarity, matching score, credential validity and successful lookup do not alone prove subject equality, control, authentication, authorization or current eligibility.
Duplicate candidates, conflicts, corrections, merges, splits, supersession and retirement are append-only, evidenced and contestable; no silent collapse or identifier reuse is permitted.

Agents may perform allowlisted reversible registration, validation and projection operations, but high-impact merges, splits, revocations, rights denials and destructive disposition require delegated authority and policy-defined confirmation.

read: Resolve Dimension policy, register profile, scheme version, access purpose, entry head, status, redirects, assurance freshness and source-qualified conflicts before use.
create: Create register identity and policy, then entry identity, external subject reference, registrar evidence and duplicate assessment before assigning identifiers.
update: Append identifier, evidence, status, match, correction, merge, split, rights or federation events with actor, authority, reason, event and knowledge time and provenance; never overwrite cited history.
delete: Apply rights, retention, legal hold and audit policy; remove eligible personal data only through authorized disposition while retaining the minimum lawful tombstone, non-reuse marker, lineage and evidence of action.

roles.name: Register owner and namespace authority
responsibilities: Own mandate, authoritative scope, identifier scheme, uniqueness and resolution contract.

roles.name: Registrar and evidence verifier
responsibilities: Create entries and bindings only under approved evidence and proofing rules.

roles.name: Subject or authorized representative
responsibilities: Receive notice and exercise applicable access, correction, objection and redress rights.

roles.name: Identity-resolution steward
responsibilities: Review duplicates, conflicts, matches, merges and splits and preserve lineage.

roles.name: Federation and interoperability steward
responsibilities: Govern cross-register trust, mappings, profile versions and loss accounting.

roles.name: Privacy, security and records steward
responsibilities: Control minimization, disclosure, redress, retention, legal hold, disposition and auditability.

roles.name: Relying party
responsibilities: Interpret scoped resolution and assurance evidence under external policy without treating it as universal truth.

access.default_rule: Deny proofing evidence, sensitive identifiers, private aliases, match features, conflicts, subject-rights records and unrestricted correlation handles; grant only the minimum current fields required by an authorized purpose.
exceptions: Registrar, subject-self, auditor, regulator, incident-response or court access cites authority and remains purpose-bound, minimum-necessary, attributable, time-limited and separately logged.
audit_requirements: Log actor, agent, role, purpose, register and entry, operation, policy, RFC 3339 time, affected assertions, source revision and outcome without copying protected evidence into the log.

read_order: Read Dimension identity, register, namespace, privacy, rights, retention, federation and agent-operation policies.
Read this pattern and linked subject, credential, account, key, policy, source-document and audit models before mutation.

coverage.claim: Covers a single-provider, source-grounded identity-register model spanning register authority and namespace rules, entry anchoring and external subject reference, identifier and alias bindings, registration and assignment evidence, assurance and quality, entry and binding lifecycle, matching, merge, split and resolution, cross-register federation and standards crosswalks, and purpose, rights, access, retention and agent governance across 6 bundles, 12 layers, 24 findings, 24 artifacts and 10 functions over 11 sources. This is not universal completeness: relationship rows are unapproved composition proposals, the composition, relationships, spatial and interoperability dimensions are self-declared gaps, ISO/IEC 24760-1 is represented at catalogue level only, question kinds are mechanically rotated rather than semantically assigned, and biometric matching, civil and population registries, eIDAS wallets, sanctions screening and sector eligibility are explicitly excluded and require separate specialist profiles.

known_omissions: No independent Claude or Grok result was available; later identity, privacy and jurisdictional review is required before canonical promotion.
No approved relation rows were supplied; relationships to person, organization, device, credential, authentication, authorization, master-data and audit models remain composition proposals.
Biometric matching, national civil identity, population registers, eIDAS wallets, sector-specific eligibility and sanctions screening require separate specialist profiles.
ISO/IEC 24760-1 is represented from the official public catalogue and sample metadata, not a licensed full-text conformity assessment.
conflicts: An identifier may be unique within one namespace yet collide or be reused under another authority or time interval.
Two entries may be similar or linked without being legally or operationally equivalent, while one subject can legitimately have multiple identities across contexts.
Privacy minimization, fraud detection, subject access, public transparency, archival duties and non-reuse can impose competing retention and disclosure requirements.
regional_assumptions: Legal identity, identifier validity, subject rights, proofing evidence, retention and redress depend on jurisdiction and sector.
NIST guidance primarily addresses persons using online services and does not establish a universal person, device or thing register.
GS1 and GLEIF define domain identifier systems; their authority and semantics must not be generalized beyond their registered subjects and rules.

The repository owner authorized completion without Grok when Grok is unavailable, slow or schema-invalid. Grok may still be attempted as a bounded supplemental reviewer, but its failure never blocks a valid Claude plus no-tools result.
